problems.title: Localization at all energies in the weakly disordered 2D Anderson model
problems.plain: Scaling theory predicts that in two dimensions every electron state is trapped by any amount of disorder, however weak. A proof exists only near the edges of the energy band or at strong disorder.
problems.precise: For $H = \Delta + \lambda V$ on $\ell^2(Z^2)$, $\Delta$ the nearest-neighbour hopping operator (spectrum $[-4, 4]$ at $\lambda = 0$), $V$ i.i.d. with bounded density (or Bernoulli), prove that for every $\lambda > 0$ the spectrum is almost surely pure point with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions at all energies, with localization length expected to grow as $\exp(c/\lambda^2)$. Answer: a proof.
problems.settled_by: A proof of complete localization for small $\lambda$ including the band center.
problems.status_note: Localization is known at large disorder and near band edges, including for Bernoulli disorder near the edge (Ding and Smart, 2020).

topic_review.cite: G. Stolz, An introduction to the mathematics of Anderson localization, Contemporary Mathematics 552, 2011 (arXiv 1104.2317)

links.reason: Monitored fermions map to sigma models whose flow mirrors two-dimensional weak localization.
Proven 2D localization at weak disorder would exclude a noninteracting 2D metal.

problems.title: Absolutely continuous spectrum of the 3D Anderson model at weak disorder
problems.plain: Prove that at least some electron states in a weakly disordered 3D lattice spread over the whole sample. This is the half of the mobility-edge problem that has no proof at all.
problems.precise: For $H = \Delta + \lambda V$ on $\ell^2(Z^3)$, with $\Delta$ the nearest-neighbour hopping operator (spectrum $[-6, 6]$ at $\lambda = 0$), i.i.d. bounded $V$ and $\lambda$ small, prove that the almost-sure spectrum has a nonzero absolutely continuous component in some energy interval inside $(-6, 6)$, or at least that eigenfunctions in that interval are not exponentially localized. Answer: a proof.
problems.settled_by: A proof of absolutely continuous spectrum, or of delocalized eigenfunctions in finite volume uniformly in the volume, for $d = 3$.
problems.status_note: Absolutely continuous spectrum at weak disorder is proven on tree graphs (Klein, 1998, and later work of Aizenman and Warzel), not on $Z^d$.

topic_review.cite: G. Stolz, An introduction to the mathematics of Anderson localization, Contemporary Mathematics 552, 2011 (arXiv 1104.2317)

problems.title: Delocalization of random band matrices in two and three dimensions
problems.plain: Random band matrices are simplified models of disordered conductors in which each site couples randomly to all sites within a distance W. The transition between trapped and spreading states in one dimension was settled in 2025, but in 2D and 3D at fixed band width it is open.
problems.precise: Hermitian random band matrices on the box $\{1..L\}^{d}$ with variance profile of width $W$. Prove for $d = 3$ that bulk eigenvectors are delocalized for $W \ge W_0$ fixed and $L \to \infty$, and for $d = 2$ that the localization length scales as $\exp(c W^2)$. Answer: proofs of these scalings.
problems.settled_by: Proofs of delocalization for fixed large $W$ in $d = 3$ and of the $\exp(c W^{2})$ localization length in $d = 2$.
problems.status_note: In $1\mathrm{D}$ the threshold $W \sim L^{1/2}$ was established in 2025 (Yau and Yin, arXiv 2501.01718; Erdos and Riabov, arXiv 2506.06441; localization by Drogin, arXiv 2508.05802); in $2\mathrm{D}$ delocalization is proven for $W \ge L^{c}$, any $c > 0$ (Dubova, Yang, Yau and Yin, arXiv 2503.07606); fixed $W$ in $d = 2, 3$ remains open.

topic_review.cite: G. Stolz, An introduction to the mathematics of Anderson localization, Contemporary Mathematics 552, 2011 (arXiv 1104.2317)

problems.title: Existence of a mobility edge in the 3D Anderson model
problems.plain: Show that in a weakly disordered 3D crystal, electrons at energies near the band edges are trapped while those in the middle of the band move freely. The boundary energy between the two regimes is the mobility edge.
problems.precise: $H = \Delta + \lambda V$ on $\ell^2(Z^3)$, with $(\Delta \psi)(x) = \sum_{\left|y-x\right|=1} \psi(y)$ the hopping operator (spectrum $[-6, 6]$ at $\lambda = 0$), $V(x)$ i.i.d. (e.g. uniform on $[-1,1]$), $\lambda > 0$ small. Prove that there is $E_c(\lambda)$ such that, almost surely, the spectrum in $\left|E\right| > E_c$ is pure point with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions and the spectrum in a nonempty interval inside $\left|E\right| < E_c$ is continuous. Answer: a proof.
problems.settled_by: A proof of coexistence of localized and delocalized spectrum for one 3D disorder distribution.
problems.status_note: Localization near band edges is proven; no delocalization result exists on $Z^d$.

topic_review.cite: G. Stolz, An introduction to the mathematics of Anderson localization, Contemporary Mathematics 552, 2011 (arXiv 1104.2317)

links.reason: Measured mobility edges test a transition whose existence is unproven for 3D models.

problems.title: Quantum diffusion for all times in the weakly disordered 3D lattice
problems.plain: An electron in a weakly disordered 3D crystal should wander like a random walker, with its mean squared distance growing linearly in time forever. This is proven only up to a long but finite time.
problems.precise: For $H = \Delta + \lambda V$ on $Z^3$, $\Delta$ the nearest-neighbour hopping operator, show that $E \sum_{x} \mid x \mid^{2} \mid \langle x \mid \mathrm{exp}(-itH) \mid 0\rangle \mid^{2} \sim D(\lambda) t$ as $t \to \infty$ with a diffusion constant $D(\lambda) > 0$ for small $\lambda$ (or the analogous statement for an energy-localized initial state). Erdos, Salmhofer and Yau proved diffusion up to times $t \sim \lambda^{-2-\kappa}$ for some $\kappa > 0$. Answer: a proof for $t \to \infty$ at fixed small $\lambda$.
problems.settled_by: A proof of diffusive spreading uniformly in time at fixed small $\lambda$.
problems.status_note: Diffusion is controlled only up to times $\lambda^{-2-\kappa}$ (Erdos, Salmhofer and Yau, around 2007-2008).

topic_review.cite: G. Stolz, An introduction to the mathematics of Anderson localization, Contemporary Mathematics 552, 2011 (arXiv 1104.2317)

problems.title: Random-matrix bulk statistics for random regular graphs of fixed degree
problems.plain: A random network in which every node has exactly d links is a discrete model of a chaotic system, and its eigenvalues should be spaced like those of random matrices. This is proven at the spectrum's edge and for slowly growing d, but not in the bulk at fixed d.
problems.precise: Adjacency matrix of a uniform random d-regular graph on $N$ vertices with $d\ge 3$ fixed. Prove that bulk local eigenvalue statistics (e.g. the gap distribution at a fixed energy inside $(-2\sqrt{d-1}, 2\sqrt{d-1})$) converge to GOE as $N\to\infty$. Answer: a proof.
problems.settled_by: A proof of GOE bulk gap or correlation universality for one fixed d.
problems.status_note: Bulk universality is proven for $N^{\alpha} \le d \le N^{2/3-\alpha}$ (Bauerschmidt, Huang, Knowles and Yau, Annals of Probability 2017, arXiv 1505.06700); at fixed d, optimal eigenvalue rigidity and Tracy-Widom edge universality were proven by Huang, McKenzie and Yau (arXiv 2412.20263, 2024).

topic_review.cite: G. Stolz, An introduction to the mathematics of Anderson localization, Contemporary Mathematics 552, 2011 (arXiv 1104.2317)

links.reason: The infinite-dimension Anderson limit is the random regular graph.
Random regular graph localization is the standard toy model of Fock-space MBL.

problems.title: Condensation of a repulsive Bose gas in the thermodynamic limit
problems.plain: Prove that a gas of mutually repelling bosons at low temperature puts a finite fraction of its particles into one quantum state when the container is infinitely large at fixed density. Without interactions this is a textbook calculation; with them there is no accepted proof.
problems.precise: $N$ bosons in a box of side $L$ in $R^{3}$, $H = \sum_i -\operatorname{Lap}_i + \sum_{i<j} v(x_i - x_j)$ with $v \ge 0$ compactly supported, density $\rho = N/L^{3}$ fixed, $L \to \infty$. Prove at $T = 0$ or at small $T > 0$ that the one-body density matrix has off-diagonal long-range order, lim_{|x-y| -> infinity} gamma^(1)(x,y) = $\rho$_0 > 0. Answer: a proof for some open range of rho and $T$.
problems.settled_by: A proof of a nonzero condensate density in the thermodynamic limit for one continuum model.
problems.status_note: Proven in the Gross-Pitaevskii scaling (Lieb and Seiringer, 2002) and for lattice hard-core bosons at half filling (Dyson, Lieb and Simon, 1978), not for continuum gases in the thermodynamic limit; a preprint by Suto (arXiv 1710.04441, 2017) claims a proof via Feynman-Kac permutation cycles and lists no journal publication.

topic_review.cite: J. P. Solovej, Mathematical physics of dilute Bose gases, arXiv, 2025

problems.title: Condensation on all length scales in the dilute Bose gas
problems.plain: In a very dilute gas the particles rarely meet, so condensation should be easiest to prove there. Current proofs work only in regions somewhat larger than the healing length, the distance over which the condensate recovers from a disturbance.
problems.precise: Dilute regime $\rho a^3 << 1$ ($a = \text{scattering length of }v$). Show that the condensate fraction in a box of side $L$ tends to $1 - O((\rho a^3)^{1/2})$ uniformly as $L \to \infty$, extending results valid for $L$ up to a power of the healing length $(8 \pi \rho a)^{-1/2}$ times a negative power of $\rho a^3$. Answer: a proof.
problems.settled_by: A proof of a condensate fraction near 1 uniform in $L$ for fixed small $\rho a^{3}$.
problems.status_note: Fournais (2021) proved condensation on length scales larger than the healing length; the infinite-volume statement is open.

topic_review.cite: J. P. Solovej, Mathematical physics of dilute Bose gases, arXiv, 2025

problems.title: Condensation of lattice hard-core bosons away from half filling
problems.plain: For bosons hopping on a 3D lattice with at most one particle per site, condensation is proven only when exactly half the sites are filled, because the proof uses a mirror symmetry that holds only there. At any other filling it is unproven.
problems.precise: Hard-core bosons on $Z^3$, H = -sum_<xy> (a_x^+ a_y + a_y^+ a_x), equivalently the spin-$1/2$ XY model in a uniform field along z, at density $\rho \text{ in } (0,1), \rho != 1/2$. Prove off-diagonal long-range order, $\lim_{\mid x-y\mid \to \infty} \langle a_x^{+} a_y\rangle > 0$, for $T$ below some $T_c(\rho) > 0$. Answer: a proof for an open interval of $\rho$.
problems.settled_by: A proof of off-diagonal long-range order at some density $\rho \ne 1/2$ that does not rely on reflection positivity.
problems.status_note: The half-filled case follows from reflection positivity (Dyson, Lieb and Simon, Journal of Statistical Physics 1978); a nonzero field breaks reflection positivity.

topic_review.cite: J. P. Solovej, Mathematical physics of dilute Bose gases, arXiv, 2025

problems.title: Shift of the condensation temperature caused by weak repulsion
problems.plain: Weak repulsion between bosons raises their condensation temperature slightly, in proportion to the interaction strength. The coefficient is known only from computer simulations.
problems.precise: For the dilute 3D Bose gas, prove that $(T_{c} - T_{c}^{0})/T_{c}^{0} = c\rho^{1/3}a + o(\rho^{1/3}a)$, with $T_{c}^{0}$ the ideal-gas value, and determine c (lattice Monte Carlo gives c approximately 1.3, Arnold and Moore; Kashurnikov, Prokof'ev and Svistunov, 2001). Answer: the existence of the phase transition and the value of c.
problems.settled_by: A proof of a phase transition at $T_{c}$ with rigorous bounds on $c$.

topic_review.cite: J. P. Solovej, Mathematical physics of dilute Bose gases, arXiv, 2025

problems.title: Third-order term in the dilute Bose gas ground-state energy
problems.plain: The energy of a dilute repulsive Bose gas is known rigorously to two terms in powers of the density. The next predicted term, with a logarithm, is proven only from above.
problems.precise: With $\hbar^{2}/(2m) = 1$, the ground-state energy density is predicted to be $e(\rho) = 4 \pi a \rho^2 [1 + (128/(15 \sqrt{\pi})) (\rho a^3)^{1/2} + 8 (4 \pi/3 - \sqrt{3}) \rho a^3 \log(\rho a^3) + o(\rho a^3 \log(\rho a^3))]$ (Wu, 1959). Prove the matching lower bound for general short-range $v \ge 0$. Answer: a proof of the two-sided expansion.
problems.settled_by: A lower bound on $e(\rho)$ matching the Wu term.
problems.status_note: The two-term Lee-Huang-Yang formula is proven (Yau and Yin 2009, upper bound; Fournais and Solovej 2020, lower bound); a third-order upper bound in the thermodynamic limit was proven by Brooks, Oldenburg, Saint Aubin and Schlein (arXiv 2506.04153, 2025).

topic_review.cite: J. P. Solovej, Mathematical physics of dilute Bose gases, arXiv, 2025

links.reason: Droplet theory needs the next term beyond Lee-Huang-Yang in the dilute Bose energy.

problems.title: Broken translation symmetry for a 3D continuum particle system
problems.plain: Prove that some realistic system of particles in continuous 3D space has, at low temperature, a thermal equilibrium state in which particles keep preferred lattice positions over infinite distances.
problems.precise: For classical particles in $R^3$ with a stable, regular pair potential $V$ (for example Lennard-Jones, or a smooth short-range potential with a crystalline ground state), prove that for large $\beta = 1/T$ at suitable density there is an infinite-volume Gibbs point process that is not translation invariant, with density correlations showing long-range periodic order. One such potential suffices.
problems.settled_by: A construction, for example by a multiscale or Pirogov-Sinai-type expansion around the crystal, of a non-translation-invariant Gibbs measure for one continuum potential in 3D.
problems.status_note: Proved for lattice models via Pirogov-Sinai theory, and positional order is ruled out for 2D continuum systems (Richthammer 2007); as of 2026 no continuum system in $d \ge 3$ has a proof of a crystalline Gibbs state.

topic_review.cite: Thomas Richthammer, Translation-invariance of two-dimensional Gibbsian point processes, Communications in Mathematical Physics, 2007

problems.title: Crystalline phase of hard spheres at high packing fraction
problems.plain: Hard balls with no attraction freeze into a crystal when packed densely enough, as computer simulations show above about 55 percent filling. Prove that such a crystalline equilibrium state exists.
problems.precise: For hard spheres of diameter $a$ in $R^3$ at packing fraction $\eta$ close to the close-packing value $\pi/\sqrt{18}$, about 0.7405, prove existence of a non-translation-invariant Gibbs measure, and more sharply a first-order freezing transition; simulations place fluid-solid coexistence at $\eta$ about 0.494 and 0.545.
problems.settled_by: A rigorous proof of crystalline long-range order for hard spheres at some $\eta$ below close packing.

topic_review.cite: Thomas Richthammer, Translation-invariance of two-dimensional Gibbsian point processes, Communications in Mathematical Physics, 2007

links.reason: Hard-sphere crystallization competes with jamming and undermines a unique random close packing.

problems.title: Existence of a hexatic phase between 2D solid and liquid
problems.plain: Theory predicts that 2D crystals melt in two steps through an intermediate hexatic phase, in which bond directions stay aligned while positions are disordered as in a liquid. Prove such a phase exists for some particle system.
problems.precise: For hard disks or a 2D system with smooth repulsion, prove existence of a range of $(T, \rho)$ where positional correlations decay exponentially while bond-orientational correlations $\langle\psi_6(x)\,\psi_6(0)*\rangle$ decay as a power law, as in the Kosterlitz-Thouless-Halperin-Nelson-Young melting scenario. Hard-disk simulations (Bernard, Krauth 2011) find a hexatic phase near packing fraction 0.70 to 0.72 with a first-order liquid-hexatic transition.
problems.settled_by: A proof of the two distinct decay laws in a nonempty parameter region of a 2D continuum model.

topic_review.cite: Thomas Richthammer, Translation-invariance of two-dimensional Gibbsian point processes, Communications in Mathematical Physics, 2007

links.reason: Two-dimensional supersolid melting may pass through hexatic order, as in particle crystals.
Skyrmion lattice melting is a test of two-step melting through a hexatic.

problems.title: Long-range bond-orientational order in 2D particle systems
problems.plain: In two dimensions thermal vibrations destroy perfect positional order, but the directions of the bonds between neighbors should still line up across the whole sample. This is proved only for simplified spring models.
problems.precise: For a 2D classical particle system with a smooth pair potential whose ground state is triangular, prove at low T a Gibbs state in which the bond-orientation field $\psi_6(x)=\sum \text{ over neighbors of } \exp(6 i \theta)$ has nonzero mean, $\theta$ the bond angle. Merkl, Rolles (2009), Heydenreich, Merkl, Rolles (2014) and Aumann (2015) prove orientational order for harmonic-spring models on a fixed triangulation, with limited or arbitrary defects; the case where particles move freely and neighbors change is open.
problems.settled_by: A proof of nonzero mean bond orientation for a genuine 2D continuum Gibbs point process at low temperature.
problems.status_note: Spring models with fixed connectivity are settled (Aumann 2015); continuum particle systems are not.

topic_review.cite: Thomas Richthammer, Translation-invariance of two-dimensional Gibbsian point processes, Communications in Mathematical Physics, 2007

problems.title: Power-law decay of positional correlations in 2D crystals
problems.plain: Theory predicts that in a 2D crystal at low temperature positional order fades slowly, as a power of distance, instead of quickly. Prove this power law for a particle system.
problems.precise: For a 2D continuum particle system with triangular ground state at low T, prove that the translational correlation $\langle \rho_G(x) \rho_G(0)*\rangle$, $G$ a reciprocal lattice vector of the triangular lattice, decays as $\mid x\mid^{-\eta_G(T)}$ with $\eta_G(T)\to 0$ as $T\to 0$ (quasi-long-range order), with matching upper and lower power-law bounds.
problems.settled_by: Upper and lower power-law bounds on positional correlations with exponent vanishing as $T \to 0$.
problems.status_note: Absence of true positional order for 2D continuum particles is proved (Richthammer 2007).

topic_review.cite: Thomas Richthammer, Translation-invariance of two-dimensional Gibbsian point processes, Communications in Mathematical Physics, 2007

problems.title: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice in the plane
problems.plain: In 2022 the $E8$ and Leech lattices were proved to be the best arrangements in 8 and 24 dimensions for every repulsive force from a broad class. The matching claim for the triangular lattice in two dimensions is unproved.
problems.precise: Prove that for every density $\rho$ the triangular lattice minimizes the energy per point $\sum_{y != x} f(\mid x - y \mid^{2})$ among all periodic configurations in $R^{2}$ of density $\rho$, for every completely monotone f (including $\exp(-a r^{2})$ and $r^{-s}$). Answer: proof or a periodic configuration beating the triangular lattice for some such f.
problems.settled_by: A proof by an interpolation or linear-programming argument in the style of the 8D and 24D case, or an explicit counterexample.
problems.status_note: Proved for $E8$ and Leech (Cohn, Kumar, Miller, Radchenko, Viazovska, Annals 2022); in 2D known only among lattices; Petrache and Serfaty (2020) showed it would imply crystallization at next order for 2D Coulomb and Riesz gases.

topic_review.cite: Xavier Blanc, Mathieu Lewin, The crystallization conjecture: a review, EMS Surveys in Mathematical Sciences, 2015

problems.title: Body-centered cubic ground state of classical 3D jellium
problems.plain: Point charges in a uniform background of opposite charge are expected to form a body-centered cubic crystal, the Wigner crystal. No proof exists that this arrangement has the lowest energy.
problems.precise: For $N$ point charges $e$ in a neutralizing uniform background of density $\rho0$ in $R^{3}$ (Coulomb $e^{2}/r$), prove that in the thermodynamic limit the minimal energy per particle equals the bcc value, about $-0.8959\,e^{2}/r_{s}$ with $r_{s}=(3/(4\pi \rho0))^{1/3}$, and that minimizers are bcc up to $o(N)$ particles. The quantum version asks the same for the electron gas as $r_{s}\to\infty$.
problems.settled_by: A proof that no configuration beats the bcc Madelung energy per particle in the thermodynamic limit.
problems.status_note: Open in both the classical and the quantum low-density version.

topic_review.cite: Xavier Blanc, Mathieu Lewin, The crystallization conjecture: a review, EMS Surveys in Mathematical Sciences, 2015

links.reason: Distillation depends on freezing of Coulomb plasma mixtures, the jellium crystal problem generalized.
Crystalline beams are one-component Coulomb plasmas ordering in a focusing lattice.

problems.title: Triangular-lattice crystallization for the 2D Lennard-Jones potential
problems.plain: In the plane, particles with Lennard-Jones forces should arrange into the triangular lattice. Existing proofs work only for forces with a much narrower attractive well.
problems.precise: For the Lennard-Jones pair potential in $R^2$, prove that $N$-particle minimizers of $E_N$ converge (energy per particle and structure away from an $o(N)$ boundary layer) to the triangular lattice with the spacing that minimizes the lattice energy. Theil's 2006 proof and its extensions (E, Li 2009) need a narrow potential well and steep core, which excludes Lennard-Jones.
problems.settled_by: An extension of the 2D crystallization proof to the Lennard-Jones potential itself.
problems.status_note: Optimality of the triangular lattice for Lennard-Jones is known only within the restricted class of Bravais lattices and for some densities.

topic_review.cite: Xavier Blanc, Mathieu Lewin, The crystallization conjecture: a review, EMS Surveys in Mathematical Sciences, 2015

problems.title: Periodic ground states for the Lennard-Jones potential in 3D
problems.plain: Prove that many particles interacting through the standard Lennard-Jones force (repulsive at short range, attractive at long range) have a lowest-energy arrangement that is a periodic crystal. Computations suggest the hexagonal close-packed crystal.
problems.precise: For $V(r)=4\epsilon ((s/r)^{12}-(s/r)^6)$, let $x_1..x_N \text{ in } R^3$ minimize $E_N=\sum_{i<j} V(\mid x_i-x_j\mid)$. Prove that $\min E_N/N$ converges to the energy per particle of one periodic configuration (expected hcp, nearly degenerate with fcc) and that minimizers, after a rigid motion, coincide with it outside a boundary layer of $o(N)$ particles. A proof for any pair potential with a repulsive core and an attractive tail in 3D would also answer the qualitative question.
problems.settled_by: A proof of convergence of $N$-particle minimizers to a periodic lattice for Lennard-Jones or a comparable two-body potential in $R^{3}$.
problems.status_note: Proved in 3D only for a tailored potential with a three-body term and fcc ground state (Flatley, Theil, ARMA 2015).

topic_review.cite: Xavier Blanc, Mathieu Lewin, The crystallization conjecture: a review, EMS Surveys in Mathematical Sciences, 2015

problems.title: Close-packed ground states of sticky hard spheres
problems.plain: Model atoms as hard balls that gain energy only when they touch. Prove that the best arrangement of many such balls stacks flat triangular layers, as in fcc or hcp crystals.
problems.precise: For $V(r)=+\infty \text{ for } r<1, -1 \text{ for } r=1, 0 \text{ for } r>1 \text{ in } R^3$, minimizing $E_N$ is maximizing the contact number $c(N)$ of $N$ non-overlapping unit-diameter spheres. Prove that for large N every minimizer coincides, except for $o(N)$ spheres, with a subset of a close packing (a stacking of triangular layers), and determine whether $\lim(6N-c(N))/N^{2/3}$ exists and, if so, its value (expected to be set by the surface energy of the optimal close-packed shape).
problems.settled_by: A structure theorem for maximal-contact configurations of N spheres together with the sharp surface constant.
problems.status_note: The 2D sticky-disk problem is solved (Heitmann, Radin 1980); in 3D only bounds on $c(N)$ of the form $6N - C N^{2/3}$ are known.

topic_review.cite: Xavier Blanc, Mathieu Lewin, The crystallization conjecture: a review, EMS Surveys in Mathematical Sciences, 2015

problems.title: Off-diagonal long-range order in a many-body model of attractive fermions
problems.plain: BCS theory explains superconductivity by electron pairing, but it is an approximation. No one has proven that a full many-electron model with attraction actually forms a pair condensate in an infinite system.
problems.precise: $N$ spin-$1/2$ fermions in a box of side $L$ with attractive short-range pair potential, density fixed, $L \to \infty$. Prove that the two-body reduced density matrix has an eigenvalue of order $N$ (Yang's off-diagonal long-range order) for $T$ below a $T_{c} > 0$, and compare $T_{c}$ with the BCS functional prediction. Answer: a proof.
problems.settled_by: A proof of pair condensation in the thermodynamic limit for the full many-body Hamiltonian.
problems.status_note: Rigorous results concern the BCS functional (Hainzl, Hamza, Seiringer and Solovej, 2008, and later) and mean-field type Hamiltonians, not the full many-body problem.

topic_review.cite: C. Hainzl, R. Seiringer, The BCS functional of superconductivity and its mathematical properties, Journal of Mathematical Physics, 2016

problems.title: Fermi-liquid behavior of weakly interacting fermions above the pairing scale
problems.plain: Show that electrons with weak repulsion in a 3D continuum act like slightly modified free particles down to very low temperatures. At the lowest temperatures they are expected to pair, so the statement must stop above that scale.
problems.precise: Spin-$1/2$ fermions in $R^{3}$ with dispersion $k^{2}/(2m)$ and weak short-range repulsion $\lambda v$. Prove that for T above the pairing scale ($T \ge \exp(-c/\lambda^{2}) E_F$, say) the momentum distribution has a jump of size $Z = 1 - \operatorname{O}(\lambda^{2})$ smeared only on scale T, and $\operatorname{Im} \Sigma(\omega, k_F) \sim \omega^{2} + (\pi T)^{2}$. Answer: a proof with explicit constants.
problems.settled_by: A convergent multiscale (renormalization-group) proof of Fermi-liquid bounds in 3D down to an exponentially small temperature.
problems.status_note: In $2\mathrm{D}$, Disertori and Rivasseau (2000) controlled jellium above an exponentially small temperature, and Feldman, Knorrer and Trubowitz (2003-2004) proved a $T = 0$ Fermi liquid for Fermi surfaces without inversion symmetry.

topic_review.cite: C. Hainzl, R. Seiringer, The BCS functional of superconductivity and its mathematical properties, Journal of Mathematical Physics, 2016

problems.title: Kohn-Luttinger superconductivity from purely repulsive interactions
problems.plain: Kohn and Luttinger argued that even purely repelling electrons pair up and superconduct at very low temperature, because the surrounding electrons screen the repulsion unevenly. This has never been proven.
problems.precise: Spin-$1/2$ fermions in $R^{3}$ (or on $Z^{2}$ at generic filling) with weak repulsive short-range v. Prove that the ground state, or the Gibbs state below some $T_c > 0$, has off-diagonal long-range order in the pair density matrix in a channel of nonzero angular momentum. Answer: a proof, with $T_c$ exponentially small in $1/\lambda$.
problems.settled_by: A proof of pair off-diagonal long-range order for a purely repulsive model.

topic_review.cite: C. Hainzl, R. Seiringer, The BCS functional of superconductivity and its mathematical properties, Journal of Mathematical Physics, 2016

links.reason: Kohn-Luttinger pairing from repulsion is a leading candidate for single-flavor graphene.
Kohn-Luttinger pairing sets the weak-coupling baseline for purely repulsive superconductivity.

problems.title: Itinerant ferromagnetism in the Hubbard model at finite hole density
problems.plain: With infinitely strong repulsion and exactly one missing electron, the Hubbard model is proven to be a ferromagnet. Whether this survives for a small but finite fraction of missing electrons is unknown.
problems.precise: Hubbard model at $U = \infty$ on $Z^{2}$ or $Z^{3}$, electron density $1 - \delta$ with hole density $\delta > 0$ small, thermodynamic limit. Prove or disprove that the ground state has total spin $S_{\mathrm{tot}}$ of order $N$ (saturated or partial ferromagnetism). Answer: yes or no with proof.
problems.settled_by: A proof of a ground state with $S_{\mathrm{tot}}$ proportional to $N$, or a variational state with lower energy and $S_{\mathrm{tot}} = o(N)$, valid in the thermodynamic limit.
problems.status_note: Nagaoka (1966) proved ferromagnetism for a single hole; flat-band models (Mielke, Tasaki) give rigorous ferromagnetism in special lattices.

topic_review.cite: C. Hainzl, R. Seiringer, The BCS functional of superconductivity and its mathematical properties, Journal of Mathematical Physics, 2016

links.reason: Triangular-lattice atom simulators have imaged kinetic Nagaoka-type magnetism around dopants.

problems.title: Regularity or blowup of axisymmetric Navier-Stokes flows with swirl
problems.plain: Flows that are symmetric around an axis but also spin around it are the leading candidates for viscous blowup. Without spin they are known to stay smooth; with spin the question is open even in this restricted class.
problems.precise: 3D Navier-Stokes on $R^{3}$ with $f = 0$ and smooth, finite-energy, axisymmetric initial data with nonzero swirl $u_{\theta}$. Prove global regularity, or give smooth axisymmetric data whose solution has $\operatorname{limsup}_{t \to T} \mid\mid u(t)\mid\mid_{\infty} = \infty$. Answer: yes or no with proof; this is a special case of mathph.fluid-singularities.ns-unforced.
problems.settled_by: A global regularity proof for all smooth axisymmetric data, or a verified (e.g. computer-assisted) blowup construction in this class without forcing.
problems.status_note: Hou (arXiv 2107.06509, Foundations of Computational Mathematics) reported numerical evidence of potentially singular axisymmetric flow with maximum vorticity growing by a factor of about $10^{7}$; regularity is proven for zero swirl (Ukhovskii and Yudovich; Ladyzhenskaya, 1968).

topic_review.cite: J. Chen, T. Y. Hou, Stable nearly self-similar blowup of the 2D Boussinesq and 3D Euler equations with smooth data I: Analysis, arXiv, 2022

problems.title: Finite-time blowup of 3D Euler from smooth data without boundaries
problems.plain: For an ideal fluid with no viscosity, it is unknown whether a smooth flow filling all of space can concentrate its rotation into infinite values in finite time. Blowup is proven when the fluid touches a wall or when the starting flow is slightly rough.
problems.precise: Incompressible Euler on $R^3$ (or $T^3$): does there exist smooth finite-energy initial data (e.g. $C_c^{\infty}$) whose solution satisfies $\int_0^T \mid\mid \omega(t)\mid\mid_{\operatorname{inf}} dt = \infty$ at a finite $T$, with $\omega = \operatorname{curl} u$ (Beale-Kato-Majda criterion)? Known: blowup for smooth data in a cylinder with boundary (Chen and Hou, computer-assisted, PNAS 2025) and for $C^{(1,\alpha)}$ data on $R^3$ (Elgindi, Annals of Mathematics 2021, small $\alpha$; Cordoba, Martinez-Zoroa and Zheng, Annals of PDE 2025). Answer: a verified construction or a proof of global regularity.
problems.settled_by: An independently verified proof, most likely a computer-assisted nonlinear stability estimate around an approximate self-similar profile.
problems.status_note: Programmatic searches in September 2026 claimed two Euler singularities (as reported by Petrillo and Glimm, arXiv 2609.23868), and Ganeshram, Duruisseaux and Anandkumar (arXiv 2609.10867) posted a candidate self-similar profile on $R^{3}$ at rate $1/2$ with a stability framework but no completed proof; none is independently verified.

problems.title: Finite-time Navier-Stokes blowup driven by a smooth force
problems.plain: A machine-generated proof announced in September 2026 claims that a viscous fluid pushed by a smooth outside force can develop infinite velocity at one point in finite time. Whether the proof is correct decides two of the four official versions of the Clay problem.
problems.precise: For $\nu > 0$, do there exist smooth divergence-free u_0 with $\mid d^a u_0(x)\mid \le C_{a,K} (1+\mid x\mid)^{-K}$ and smooth f with $\mid d_x^a d_t^m f\mid \le C_{a,m,K} (1+\mid x\mid+t)^{-K}$ for which no smooth finite-energy solution of forced 3D Navier-Stokes exists on $R^3 x [0, \infty)$ (Clay statement C; statement D is the periodic version)? The OpenAI construction claims such a blowup; its structure, as abstracted by Constantin, Ignatova and Vicol (arXiv 2609.20803), is Type II with an anisotropic angular mean and exact axisymmetry in a core collapsing to the singular point. Answer: independent verification or a located error.
problems.settled_by: A line-by-line check of the manuscript and of any accompanying formal proof, including a check that the formal definitions match the Clay statement.
problems.status_note: Announced by OpenAI on 7-8 September 2026 (dates as reported by Petrillo and Glimm, arXiv 2609.23868); Constantin, Ignatova and Vicol (arXiv 2609.20803) proved rigidity constraints on constructions of its type; no independent verification as of 2026-10-01.

topic_review.cite: J. Chen, T. Y. Hou, Stable nearly self-similar blowup of the 2D Boussinesq and 3D Euler equations with smooth data I: Analysis, arXiv, 2022

problems.title: Uniqueness of Leray-Hopf weak solutions without forcing
problems.plain: Weak solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations, which satisfy the equations only in an averaged sense, always exist, but it is unknown whether they are unique when no outside force acts. With a specially designed force, two different solutions from the same start are known.
problems.precise: 3D Navier-Stokes on $R^{3}$ with $f = 0$ and divergence-free $u_{0}$ in $L^{2}$: is the Leray-Hopf weak solution ($u\ \text{in}\ L^{\infty}_{t} L^{2}_{x}$ and $L^{2}_{t} H^{1}_{x}$, satisfying the energy inequality) unique? Albritton, Brue and Colombo proved non-uniqueness for a force $f\ \text{in}\ L^{1}_{t} L^{2}_{x}$ built from an unstable self-similar profile. Answer: yes or no with proof.
problems.settled_by: A proof of uniqueness for all $L^{2}$ data, or two distinct Leray-Hopf solutions from the same data with $f = 0$.
problems.status_note: Non-uniqueness with forcing was shown by Albritton, Brue and Colombo (Annals of Mathematics, 2022); the unforced case remains open.

topic_review.cite: J. Chen, T. Y. Hou, Stable nearly self-similar blowup of the 2D Boussinesq and 3D Euler equations with smooth data I: Analysis, arXiv, 2022

problems.title: Global regularity or blowup of unforced 3D Navier-Stokes flows
problems.plain: Prove that every smooth, finite-energy flow of a viscous incompressible fluid in 3D stays smooth forever, or find one that develops infinite velocity in finite time with no outside push. This is the unforced half of the Clay Millennium problem.
problems.precise: Incompressible Navier-Stokes $\mathrm{d}u/\mathrm{d}t + (u.\mathrm{grad})u = \nu\,\mathrm{Lap}\,u - \mathrm{grad}\,p, \mathrm{div}\,u = 0$, on $R^3$ or the torus $T^3$ with $\nu > 0$, external force $f = 0$ and smooth divergence-free initial data (Schwartz class on $R^3$). Answer: a proof that the smooth solution exists for all $t > 0$ (Clay statements A and B), or smooth data whose solution has $\operatorname{limsup}_{t \to T} \mid\mid u(t)\mid\mid_{\infty} = \infty$ at a finite $T$.
problems.settled_by: A refereed, independently checked proof of global regularity or an explicit blowup construction with $f = 0$.
problems.status_note: OpenAI announced in September 2026 a blowup with a smooth time-dependent force (Clay statements C and D); Constantin, Ignatova and Vicol (arXiv 2609.20803, 2026) proved that for constructions of that type (anisotropic Type II angular mean, exactly axisymmetric collapsing core) the force can neither vanish identically near the singular point nor be real analytic in space, so such constructions cannot be made unforced.

topic_review.cite: J. Chen, T. Y. Hou, Stable nearly self-similar blowup of the 2D Boussinesq and 3D Euler equations with smooth data I: Analysis, arXiv, 2022

problems.title: Finite-time singularity of the inviscid surface quasi-geostrophic equation
problems.plain: The surface quasi-geostrophic equation describes temperature carried by a flow it drives itself, and it behaves like a two-dimensional version of the 3D Euler equations. Whether a smooth temperature pattern can form an infinitely sharp front in finite time is unknown.
problems.precise: Inviscid SQG: $\mathrm{d}\theta/\mathrm{d}t + u . \mathrm{grad}\,\theta = 0$, $u = (-R_2 \theta, R_1 \theta)$ with $R_j$ the Riesz transforms, on $R^2$ or $T^2$, smooth (e.g. $C_c^\infty$) initial $\theta$, no forcing. Prove global regularity, or give smooth data with $\int_{0}^{T} ||\mathrm{grad}\,\theta(t)||_{\mathrm{inf}}\,\mathrm{d}t = \infty$ at finite T. Answer: yes or no with proof.
problems.settled_by: A proof of global regularity or a verified finite-time singularity from smooth finite-energy data without forcing.
problems.status_note: Frontal blowup was proposed by Constantin, Majda and Tabak (1994); blowup from smooth compactly supported data with a suitable time-dependent force, inside the Sobolev well-posedness regime, was proven for generalized SQG with $\gamma \text{ in } (0,1)$ (Cordoba, Dominguez, Lucas-Manchon and Martinez-Zoroa, arXiv 2608.17192, 2026), not for unforced SQG.

topic_review.cite: J. Chen, T. Y. Hou, Stable nearly self-similar blowup of the 2D Boussinesq and 3D Euler equations with smooth data I: Analysis, arXiv, 2022

problems.title: Rigorous unstable self-similar singularities in incompressible fluid models
problems.plain: Computer searches in 2025 found self-similar blowup solutions that occur only for finely tuned starting flows (unstable singularities) in simpler 2D fluid models. Turning these numerical profiles into proofs is open.
problems.precise: Wang et al. (arXiv 2509.14185, 2025) computed families of unstable self-similar profiles to high precision for the Cordoba-Cordoba-Fontelos model, the 2D incompressible porous media equation and the 2D Boussinesq equations with boundary. Prove that at least one such profile yields an exact finite-time singularity from smooth data, by a computer-assisted stability estimate on the finite-codimension set of data attracted to it. Answer: a proof for each profile family.
problems.settled_by: A computer-assisted proof of nonlinear stability modulo finitely many unstable directions for one profile of the unforced equations.
problems.status_note: Profiles were computed numerically in 2025; a rigorous stability proof was the stated next step.

problems.title: Atomic radius bounded independently of nuclear charge
problems.plain: Heavy atoms are about the same size as light ones, roughly $10^{-8}$ cm across. Prove from the many-electron Schrodinger equation that the size of a neutral atom does not grow with Z.
problems.precise: For a neutral ground state $\psi$ of $H_{Z,Z}$ with one-electron density $\rho$, define $R(Z)$ as the radius with $\int_{|x|>R(Z)}\rho(x)\,dx=1$. Prove $c a_0\le R(Z)\le C a_0$ with $a_0=\hbar^2/(m e^2)$ and constants c, C independent of Z, or show R(Z) grows or shrinks without bound.
problems.settled_by: Z-independent upper and lower bounds on R(Z) for the neutral many-body ground state.
problems.status_note: Proved in Hartree-Fock theory (Solovej 2003); open for the Schrodinger Hamiltonian.

topic_review.cite: Phan Thanh Nam, The ionization problem in quantum mechanics, in The Physics and Mathematics of Elliott Lieb (EMS Press), 2022

problems.title: Excess electron number of atoms bounded independently of nuclear charge
problems.plain: Show that there is one fixed number C such that no atom, however heavy, can bind more than Z + C electrons. Bind means the extra electrons stay attached instead of flying off to infinity.
problems.precise: For $H_{N,Z} = \sum_{i=1}^N (-\hbar^2/(2m) \Delta_i - Z e^2/|x_i|) + \sum_{i<j} e^2/|x_i - x_j|$ on antisymmetric $L^2((R^3 x \{\mathrm{up},\mathrm{down}\})^N)$ with a static point nucleus, let $E(N,Z)$ be its ground-state energy and $N_c(Z)$ the largest N with $E(N,Z) < E(N-1,Z)$. Prove or disprove $N_c(Z) \le Z + C$ with C independent of Z. Answer: a proof with explicit or existential C, or a sequence $Z_k$ with $N_c(Z_k) - Z_k$ unbounded.
problems.settled_by: A proof that bounds $N_{c}(Z) - Z$ uniformly in $Z$, for example by controlling the screened nuclear potential felt by the outermost electrons in the many-body ground state.
problems.status_note: Best known: $N_{c} < 2Z + 1$ (Lieb 1984), $N_{c} < 1.22 Z + 3 Z^{1/3}$ (Nam 2012), $N_{c}/Z \to 1$ (Lieb, Sigal, Simon, Thirring 1988) and $N_{c} - Z \le C Z^{5/7}$ for large Z (Fefferman, Seco 1990; Seco, Sigal, Solovej 1990); the bounded-excess statement is proved in Hartree-Fock theory (Solovej, Annals 2003) and in Thomas-Fermi-Dirac-von Weizsacker theory (Frank, Nam, Van Den Bosch, CPAM 2018), not for the Schrodinger Hamiltonian.

topic_review.cite: Phan Thanh Nam, The ionization problem in quantum mechanics, in The Physics and Mathematics of Elliott Lieb (EMS Press), 2022

problems.title: Uniform bound on the ionization energy of neutral atoms
problems.plain: The energy needed to remove one electron from a neutral atom is a few eV for every element in the periodic table. Prove that it stays bounded as Z grows.
problems.precise: Let $I(Z) = E(Z-1,Z) - E(Z,Z)$ for the Hamiltonian $H_{N,Z}$ of mathph.ionization.excess-charge-bound. Prove $\operatorname{sup}_Z I(Z) < \infty$, i.e. $I(Z) \le C m e^4/\hbar^2$ with $C$ independent of $Z$, or show $I(Z)$ is unbounded.
problems.settled_by: A Z-independent upper bound on E(Z-1,Z) - E(Z,Z) derived for the full many-electron Hamiltonian.
problems.status_note: Proved in Hartree-Fock theory (Solovej 2003); for the Schrodinger Hamiltonian the best known bound grows with $Z, I(Z) \le C Z^{5/7}$ (Seco, Sigal, Solovej 1990).

topic_review.cite: Phan Thanh Nam, The ionization problem in quantum mechanics, in The Physics and Mathematics of Elliott Lieb (EMS Press), 2022

problems.title: Excess charge of molecules bounded by a constant per nucleus
problems.plain: A molecule with several nuclei can also hold extra electrons. Show that the number of extra electrons is at most a fixed constant times the number of nuclei, whatever the nuclear charges and positions.
problems.precise: For $K$ static nuclei with charges $Z_1, ..., Z_K$ at positions $R_1, ..., R_K$, $Z_{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_k Z_k$, and $N$ electrons with Coulomb interactions, let $N_c$ be the largest N for which the electronic ground state is bound. Prove $N_c \le Z_{\mathrm{tot}} + C K$ with C independent of the $Z_{k}$, $R_{k}$ and K, or give a counterexample family.
problems.settled_by: A proof of the bound uniform in nuclear charges and positions, or an explicit configuration violating it.
problems.status_note: Lieb's 1984 bound $N_c < 2 Z_{\mathrm{tot}} + K$ holds for all nuclear positions.

topic_review.cite: Phan Thanh Nam, The ionization problem in quantum mechanics, in The Physics and Mathematics of Elliott Lieb (EMS Press), 2022

problems.title: No atom binds two extra electrons
problems.plain: Experiments find no stable atom carrying two extra electrons. Prove from the Schrodinger equation that $N_c(Z) \le Z + 1$ for every element.
problems.precise: With $H_{N,Z}$ and $N_c(Z)$ as in mathph.ionization.excess-charge-bound (static nucleus, nonrelativistic, spin $1/2$ electrons), prove $N_c(Z) \le Z + 1$ for all $Z \ge 1$, or exhibit $Z$ with $N_c(Z) \ge Z + 2$. A computer-assisted proof for small $Z$ combined with an asymptotic argument for large $Z$ would count.
problems.settled_by: A proof that $E(N, Z) = E(N-1, Z)$ for every $N \ge Z + 2$ and every $Z$, i.e. that no ion with two or more extra electrons has a bound ground state.
problems.status_note: Lieb's bound $N_c < 2Z + 1$ gives this statement only for hydrogen ($Z = 1$); no stable doubly charged atomic negative ion has been observed.

topic_review.cite: Phan Thanh Nam, The ionization problem in quantum mechanics, in The Physics and Mathematics of Elliott Lieb (EMS Press), 2022

problems.title: Rotational and conformal invariance of the critical 3D Ising scaling limit
problems.plain: At its critical point the 3D Ising model is believed to look the same under rotations and angle-preserving maps (conformal symmetry), which physicists use to compute exponents. In 2D this was proven; in 3D even rotation invariance is unproven.
problems.precise: Show that the scaling limit of critical spin correlations on $Z^3$ exists, is rotation invariant, and transforms covariantly under conformal maps of $R^3$ with scaling dimension $\Delta_{\sigma}\ \text{approximately}\ 0.51815$. Answer: a proof.
problems.settled_by: A proof of rotation invariance of the 3D scaling limit, then of conformal covariance.
problems.status_note: Conformal invariance in 2D was proven by Smirnov (2010) and by Chelkak, Hongler and Izyurov (2015).

topic_review.cite: H. Duminil-Copin, 100 years of the (critical) Ising model on the hypercubic lattice, arXiv, 2022

links.reason: Proven conformal invariance would justify bootstrap determinations of 3D Ising exponents.

problems.title: Existence of critical exponents for the 3D Ising model
problems.plain: Prove that quantities such as the decay of spin correlations at the critical temperature follow exact power laws in 3D. Their numerical values are known very precisely, but even their existence is unproven.
problems.precise: Nearest-neighbour Ising model on $Z^3$ at $\beta_c$. Prove that $\langle s_0 s_x\rangle_{\beta_c}=\left|x\right|^{-(1+\eta)+o(1)}$ and that the correlation length $\xi(\beta)=(\beta_c-\beta)^{-\nu+o(1)}$, with numerical values $\eta\ \mathrm{approximately}\ 0.0363$ and $\nu\ \mathrm{approximately}\ 0.6300$. Answer: a proof of existence of the limits, with or without their values.
problems.settled_by: A proof that the exponents $\eta$ and $\nu$ exist as limits.
problems.status_note: Continuity of the phase transition in 3D was proven by Aizenman, Duminil-Copin and Sidoravicius (2015).

topic_review.cite: H. Duminil-Copin, 100 years of the (critical) Ising model on the hypercubic lattice, arXiv, 2022

problems.title: Logarithmic corrections at the critical point of the 4D Ising model
problems.plain: In four dimensions the critical Ising model is almost free, and its quantities deviate from simple power laws only by slowly varying logarithms with predicted powers. These powers are proven for related weakly interacting models but not for the Ising model itself.
problems.precise: Nearest-neighbour Ising model on $Z^4$. Prove $\chi(\beta)\sim C(\beta_c-\beta)^{-1}\left|\log(\beta_c-\beta)\right|^{1/3}$ as $\beta\to \beta_c^{-}$ (the $n=1$ case of the exponent $(n+2)/(n+8)$), and the corresponding corrections for the correlation length and specific heat. Answer: a proof.
problems.settled_by: A proof of the $\mid\log\mid^{1/3}$ susceptibility correction for the nearest-neighbour 4D Ising model.
problems.status_note: Aizenman and Duminil-Copin (Annals of Mathematics, 2021, arXiv 1912.07973) proved Gaussian scaling limits with a logarithmic improvement of the tree bound; exact logarithmic exponents are proven for weakly coupled $4\mathrm{D}$ $\mid\phi\mid^{4}$ and weakly self-avoiding walk (Bauerschmidt, Brydges and Slade, 2014-2015).

topic_review.cite: H. Duminil-Copin, 100 years of the (critical) Ising model on the hypercubic lattice, arXiv, 2022

problems.title: Non-Gaussian scaling limit of the critical 3D Ising model
problems.plain: In four or more dimensions the critical Ising model looks like a free (Gaussian) field at large scales. In 3D it should not, and this difference is unproven.
problems.precise: Prove that every subsequential scaling limit of the critical spin field on $Z^{3}$ is non-Gaussian, for example that the rescaled fourth Ursell function does not vanish, and that $\eta > 0$ strictly (the infrared bound gives only $\eta \ge 0$). Answer: a proof.
problems.settled_by: A proof of a nonvanishing four-point Ursell function in the 3D scaling limit.
problems.status_note: Gaussianity is proven for $d \ge 5$ (Aizenman; Frohlich, 1982) and $d = 4$ (Aizenman and Duminil-Copin, 2021).

topic_review.cite: H. Duminil-Copin, 100 years of the (critical) Ising model on the hypercubic lattice, arXiv, 2022

problems.title: Endpoint-distance exponent of the 3D self-avoiding walk
problems.plain: A random path that never visits the same point twice models a polymer chain, and in 3D its size should grow as the number of steps to the power 0.588. Even a power-law improvement over straight-line growth is unproven.
problems.precise: Self-avoiding walk on $Z^3$ with $n$ steps, uniform measure. Prove $\langle \mid w(n)\mid^2\rangle^{1/2} = n^{\nu+o(1)}$ with $\nu\ \text{approximately}\ 0.5876$, or at least $\langle \mid w(n)\mid^2\rangle^{1/2} \le n^{1-\delta}$ for some $\delta > 0$. Answer: a proof.
problems.settled_by: A polynomial sub-ballistic bound, then existence of $\nu$.
problems.status_note: Sub-ballistic behavior $o(n)$ is proven (Duminil-Copin and Hammond, 2013); in $d = 4$ weakly self-avoiding walk has proven logarithmic corrections (Bauerschmidt, Brydges and Slade).

topic_review.cite: H. Duminil-Copin, 100 years of the (critical) Ising model on the hypercubic lattice, arXiv, 2022

problems.title: Optimal diffusion time compared with the Nekhoroshev stability bound
problems.plain: Nekhoroshev proved that drift in nearly regular systems takes at least an exponentially long time. Whether typical systems actually drift that fast, and with which exponent, is open.
problems.precise: For analytic $H = h(I) + \epsilon f$ with $h$ convex in $n$ degrees of freedom, Nekhoroshev gives $\left|I(t) - I(0)\right| \le C \epsilon^b$ for $\left|t\right| \le \exp(c \epsilon^{-a})$ with optimal $a = 1/(2n)$. Prove that for generic $f$ there are orbits drifting by order one in time $\exp(C \epsilon^{-1/(2n)})$, matching the upper bound. Answer: a proof of the matching lower bound or a counter-argument.
problems.settled_by: A construction of diffusing orbits with time $\exp(C \epsilon^{-1/(2n)})$ for an open set of perturbations.
problems.status_note: Specific analytic perturbations with diffusion time exponentially long in a power of 1/eps near the Nekhoroshev exponent were built by Ke Zhang (Inventiones Mathematicae, 2011); matching bounds for generic f are open.

problems.title: Generic Lyapunov instability of elliptic equilibria in many degrees of freedom
problems.plain: At an equilibrium where all nearby motions oscillate, orbits that start very close may still drift away very slowly. This is expected for typical systems with three or more degrees of freedom, but it is proven only for special constructions and for five or more degrees of freedom.
problems.precise: Real-analytic $H$ on $R^{2n}$, $n \ge 3$, with $H = \sum_i \omega_i (p_i^2 + q_i^2)/2 + O(3)$, $\omega$ non-resonant and not all $\omega_i$ of one sign. Prove that the origin is Lyapunov unstable for generic higher-order terms (open dense or residual set in a suitable analytic topology). Answer: a proof, or a stable open set of examples.
problems.settled_by: A proof of generic Lyapunov instability for some $n \ge 3$ among all real-analytic Hamiltonians with given quadratic part.
problems.status_note: Fayad (arXiv 1809.09059, 2018) gave explicit real entire unstable examples in four or more degrees of freedom; Fayad, Paradela, Saprykina and Seara (arXiv 2609.03722, 2026) proved that for $n \ge 5$ any analytic Hamiltonian with a locally integrable non-degenerate elliptic equilibrium of indefinite quadratic part can be analytically perturbed to an unstable one; $n = 3, 4$ and full genericity remain open.

topic_review.cite: V. Kaloshin, K. Zhang, Arnold Diffusion for Smooth Systems of Two and a Half Degrees of Freedom, Annals of Mathematics Studies 208, Princeton University Press, 2020

problems.title: Arnold diffusion for generic nearly integrable systems
problems.plain: Arnold conjectured that in typical nearly regular systems with three or more degrees of freedom, some orbits drift by a finite amount no matter how small the perturbation. This is proven only in a weaker sense of typical, or for low numbers of degrees of freedom.
problems.precise: $H = h(I) + \varepsilon f(\theta, I)$, $(\theta, I)\ \mathrm{in}\ T^{n} x R^{n}$, h strictly convex, $n \ge 3$. Prove that for generic f (residual in $C^r$, r large; separately, for an open set of analytic f) and all small $\varepsilon > 0$ there are orbits with $\mid I(T) - I(0) \mid \ge c$ with c independent of $\varepsilon$. Answer: a proof for every $n \ge 3$.
problems.settled_by: A proof valid for arbitrary n with residual (or analytic open) genericity.
problems.status_note: Proven for two and a half degrees of freedom for cusp-residual $C^r$ perturbations (Kaloshin and Zhang, Annals of Mathematics Studies 2020; Cheng); arbitrary n in a weaker cusp-residual sense (Bernard, Kaloshin and Zhang, Acta Mathematica 2016); genuinely residual or analytic perturbations remain open.

problems.title: KAM tori for the planetary N-body problem with actual masses
problems.plain: KAM theory proves that planetary systems have many stable quasi-periodic orbits, but only for planets far lighter than real ones. Proving the same with the actual masses of Jupiter and Saturn is open.
problems.precise: Planetary N-body problem (Sun plus planets with mass ratios $\mu$). Arnold (1963) and Fejoz (2004) proved positive-measure sets of KAM tori for $\mu$ below an unspecified tiny threshold. Prove existence of invariant tori near the observed orbits for the actual $\mu \sim 10^{-3}$ of the Sun-Jupiter-Saturn system, for example by computer-assisted KAM. Answer: a proof.
problems.settled_by: A computer-assisted KAM proof for the full (non-truncated) planar or spatial Sun-Jupiter-Saturn problem with real parameters.
problems.status_note: Computer-assisted KAM has been done for truncated secular models of Sun-Jupiter-Saturn (Locatelli and Giorgilli, 2000s); Capinski and Gidea (arXiv 2504.09273, 2025) gave a computer-assisted proof of Arnold diffusion in the planar full three-body problem.
