problems.title: When do non-invertible symmetries forbid a featureless gapped phase?
problems.plain: Some symmetries force a theory to have massless particles or a degenerate vacuum. A test telling which non-invertible symmetries do this exists only in two dimensions.
problems.precise: For a QFT with a finite non-invertible symmetry $C$, find a computable criterion on $C$ that decides whether a trivially gapped, symmetric, non-degenerate phase is possible. In 2D the criterion is the existence of a fiber functor for the fusion category $C$; find the analogue in $d=3 \text{ and } 4$.
problems.settled_by: A theorem stating the criterion for $d = 3, 4$ with examples where it forces gaplessness or degeneracy.
problems.status_note: Settled in $2\mathrm{D}$ (2018-2023); open in $d \ge 3$.

topic_review.cite: S. Schafer-Nameki, ICTP Lectures on (Non-)Invertible Generalized Symmetries, arXiv:2305.18296, 2023

links.reason: Emergent anomalies that forbid trivial gapped phases underlie intrinsically gapless topological phases.

problems.title: Sharp distinction between Higgs and confining phases with fundamental matter
problems.plain: With quarks present, the usual test for confinement fails, and the confining phase and the Higgs phase (where a condensed field gives the force carriers mass) seem smoothly connected. Whether some generalized symmetry or order parameter still separates them is unknown.
problems.precise: With dynamical matter in the fundamental representation, the $Z_N$ one-form center symmetry is explicitly broken and the Wilson-loop area law is no longer an order parameter; Fradkin and Shenker (1979) showed the phases can be connected. Determine whether, in theories with additional global symmetries (for example a $U(1)$ broken in both regimes, as in dense QCD), a vortex-holonomy or other non-local order parameter sharply separates Higgs and confining phases, and whether this holds generally.
problems.settled_by: A proof that the proposed order parameter is quantized and differs between the phases, confirmed by lattice simulation of a model with a phase transition along every path.
problems.status_note: Cherman, Jacobson, Sen and Yaffe (2020-2024) proposed a vortex-holonomy order parameter; its validity is disputed, and lattice studies (2023-2025) report gauge-independent transitions in SU(2) gauge-scalar models.

topic_review.cite: S. Schafer-Nameki, ICTP Lectures on (Non-)Invertible Generalized Symmetries, arXiv:2305.18296, 2023

problems.title: Observable consequences of non-invertible symmetries in the Standard Model
problems.plain: Some symmetries of the Standard Model, thought to be destroyed by quantum effects, survive in a form with no undo. Which measurable predictions follow from them is unclear.
problems.precise: The ABJ-anomalous axial U(1) symmetries of QED and of the Standard Model retain non-invertible rational-angle subgroups (Choi, Lam, Shao 2022; Cordova, Ohmori 2022). Determine the exact selection rules and constraints on observables (neutral pion decay, axion couplings, neutrino masses) that follow from them beyond ordinary anomaly matching.
problems.settled_by: A derivation of an exact constraint on a measurable quantity that follows from the non-invertible symmetry and not from ordinary anomaly matching.

topic_review.cite: S. Schafer-Nameki, ICTP Lectures on (Non-)Invertible Generalized Symmetries, arXiv:2305.18296, 2023

links.reason: Non-invertible chiral symmetries have been proposed to solve the strong CP problem.

problems.title: Mathematical structure of finite generalized symmetries above two dimensions
problems.plain: In two dimensions all finite symmetries, including those without an undo, are described by a known algebraic structure. In higher dimensions the right structure is conjectured but not established.
problems.precise: In $2\mathrm{D}$, finite internal symmetries are fusion categories. In d dimensions finite generalized symmetries are conjectured to be fusion $\left(d-1\right)$-categories, equivalently a $\left(d+1\right)$-dimensional topological field theory (the symmetry TFT) with a gapped boundary. Determine whether every finite generalized symmetry of a d-dimensional QFT arises from a symmetry TFT in this way, and classify the possible structures for $d = 3\ \text{and}\ 4$.
problems.settled_by: A proof that any finite collection of topological defects in a $d$-dimensional QFT defines a symmetry TFT with gapped boundary, together with a classification for $d = 3, 4$.
problems.status_note: The symmetry TFT framework was developed in 2021-2025; classification of fusion higher categories is incomplete.

topic_review.cite: S. Schafer-Nameki, ICTP Lectures on (Non-)Invertible Generalized Symmetries, arXiv:2305.18296, 2023

problems.title: How negative can forward-limit coefficients be once gravity is included?
problems.plain: Without gravity, a certain coefficient in the scattering of two particles must be positive. With gravity it may be slightly negative, and the size of the allowed negative value is not known.
problems.precise: For a weakly coupled 4D effective field theory of a massless scalar coupled to Einstein gravity, with $2\to 2$ amplitude $M(s,t) = 8\pi G s^2/(-t) + c_2 s^2/\Lambda^4 + ...$, determine the lowest value of $c_2$ consistent with unitarity, analyticity, crossing and a UV completion whose amplitude Reggeizes (grows as $s^{2 + \alpha' t}$) above a scale $M_*$. Under this Regge assumption proposals give $c_2 \ge -\operatorname{O}(\Lambda^4/(M_{\mathrm{pl}}^2 M_*^2))$; smeared impact-parameter sum rules in $D = 4$ instead give $c_2 \ge -\operatorname{O}(G \Lambda^4/M^2)\log(M b_{\mathrm{IR}})$, where $M$ is the EFT cutoff and $b_{\mathrm{IR}}$ an infrared impact-parameter cutoff. An answer is the optimal bound in $D = 4$ with its assumptions stated, saying which form is optimal, or an explicit consistent UV completion that violates it.
problems.settled_by: A derivation from stated axioms of the optimal lower bound on $c_{2}$, checked against explicit string-theory amplitudes.
problems.status_note: Bounds allowing Planck-suppressed negativity have been derived since 2020, but their size depends on the assumed Regge behavior of the UV completion or on an infrared cutoff.

topic_review.cite: C. de Rham, S. Kundu, M. Reece, A. J. Tolley, S.-Y. Zhou, Snowmass White Paper: UV Constraints on IR Physics, arXiv:2203.06805, 2022

links.reason: Positivity bounds with gravity restrict the parameter space of massive gravity.

problems.title: Bounds on four-dimensional gravitational couplings free of infrared logarithms
problems.plain: In four dimensions, the known bounds that account for gravity depend, through a logarithm, on an arbitrary largest distance, because gravity's pull falls off too slowly. A version free of this dependence is not known.
problems.precise: Dispersive bounds on 4D gravitational EFT coefficients (for example $R^3$ and $R^4$ corrections to Einstein gravity) obtained from smeared impact-parameter sum rules hold only up to a factor $\log(b_{\mathrm{IR}} M)$, where $b_{\mathrm{IR}}$ is an infrared impact-parameter cutoff and $M$ the EFT cutoff (Caron-Huot, Li, Parra-Martinez, Simmons-Duffin, JHEP 05 (2023) 122). Find an infrared-safe observable whose sum rules give bounds independent of $b_{\mathrm{IR}}$, or prove that the logarithm cannot be removed.
problems.settled_by: A 4D sum rule built from infrared-finite quantities that yields cutoff-independent bounds, or a no-go theorem.
problems.status_note: Bounds valid up to the infrared logarithm were derived in 2022; cutoff-independent versions are not established.

topic_review.cite: C. de Rham, S. Kundu, M. Reece, A. J. Tolley, S.-Y. Zhou, Snowmass White Paper: UV Constraints on IR Physics, arXiv:2203.06805, 2022

problems.title: Does electromagnetism plus gravity require new particles far below the Planck scale?
problems.plain: Applying positivity rules to electrons and photons with gravity seems to demand new particles at an energy far below the Planck scale (the energy where quantum gravity becomes strong). It is unsettled whether this is a real prediction or an artifact of how the graviton contribution is handled.
problems.precise: For QED with electron mass $m_{e}$ and charge $e$ coupled to gravity, the one-loop light-by-light and gravitational contributions to the forward photon-photon amplitude violate the naive positivity bound unless new states appear at $\Lambda_{\mathrm{new}}\sim(e\,m_{e}\,M_{\mathrm{pl}})^{1/2}$, approximately $2 \times 10^{7}\ \text{to}\ 4 \times 10^{7}\ \mathrm{GeV}$ (reduced or unreduced Planck mass) (Alberte, de Rham, Jaitly, Tolley, Phys. Rev. D 103, 125020, 2021, obtained assuming the t-channel graviton pole can be discarded). Decide whether every consistent UV completion of QED plus gravity has new states below this scale, or whether the allowed Planck-suppressed negativity removes the requirement.
problems.settled_by: A rigorous gravitational positivity bound with controlled negativity, evaluated on the one-loop QED plus gravity amplitude.
problems.status_note: Alberte, de Rham, Jaitly, Tolley (arXiv Dec 2020, PRD 2021) derived the low scale only under the assumption that the t-channel pole may be discarded, and conjectured that allowed negativity removes it; unresolved as of 2026.

topic_review.cite: C. de Rham, S. Kundu, M. Reece, A. J. Tolley, S.-Y. Zhou, Snowmass White Paper: UV Constraints on IR Physics, arXiv:2203.06805, 2022

problems.title: Prove high-energy growth bound for gravitational amplitudes from first principles
problems.plain: All positivity arguments assume that scattering amplitudes do not grow too fast at high energy. For gravity this growth limit is assumed, not proven.
problems.precise: Prove that the $2 \to 2$ amplitude of a consistent quantum gravity theory satisfies $M(s,t)/s^{2} \to 0\ \text{as}\ s \to \infty\ \text{at fixed}\ t < 0$ (so dispersion relations with two subtractions hold), using only unitarity, analyticity, crossing and polynomial or subexponential boundedness, in $D \ge 4$. Haring and Zhiboedov (2022) derived this bound with the extra assumption that scattering at large impact parameter is controlled by known semiclassical physics; justifying or removing that assumption, and handling $D = 4$ infrared divergences, is the open part.
problems.settled_by: A proof of the $s^{2}$ bound from axioms that do not assume semiclassical large-impact-parameter behavior, or a counterexample amplitude.
problems.status_note: The 2022 derivation rests on the semiclassical large-impact-parameter assumption.

topic_review.cite: C. de Rham, S. Kundu, M. Reece, A. J. Tolley, S.-Y. Zhou, Snowmass White Paper: UV Constraints on IR Physics, arXiv:2203.06805, 2022

problems.title: Infrared phase of strongly coupled chiral gauge theories
problems.plain: Theories where left and right particles feel the force differently can become strongly interacting at long distances. Whether they then confine with massless composite particles or break their symmetries is unknown.
problems.precise: For asymptotically free 4D chiral gauge theories such as SU(5) with fermions in 5bar + 10, or the Bars-Yankielowicz and Georgi-Glashow families, determine the infrared phase: confinement with massless composite fermions saturating 't Hooft anomalies, dynamical Higgsing (tumbling, color-flavor locking), or an IR CFT.
problems.settled_by: Nonperturbative simulation of the theory, which requires a lattice chiral regularization, or anomaly arguments that exclude all but one phase.
problems.status_note: Generalized-anomaly arguments (2019-2025) constrain but do not fix the phase.

topic_review.cite: M. Luscher, Chiral gauge theories revisited, Subnucl. Ser. 38, 41, 2002

problems.title: Can interactions decouple mirror fermions in lattice chiral theories?
problems.plain: Grid versions of fermions come with unwanted partner particles of opposite handedness, called mirror fermions. The proposal is to make the mirrors heavy with strong interactions and leave the wanted particles massless.
problems.precise: In mirror-fermion or domain-wall lattice formulations of an anomaly-free chiral theory, add interactions that gap the mirror sector by symmetric mass generation while the target sector stays massless. Determine whether, after weak gauging, the continuum limit is the target chiral gauge theory with no extra massless states and no fermion propagator zeros that act as ghost-like states. Minimal test case: the 2D U(1) 3-4-5-0 model of Wang and Wen.
problems.settled_by: A lattice computation in the 3-4-5-0 model, then in 4D, showing the gauged mirror sector decouples with a unitary spectrum, or a proof that propagator zeros are unavoidable.
problems.status_note: Golterman and Shamir (2023-2026) argue that symmetric mass generation produces propagator zeros that spoil the gauged theory; numerical tests in 2D continued in 2026.

topic_review.cite: M. Luscher, Chiral gauge theories revisited, Subnucl. Ser. 38, 41, 2002

problems.title: Gauge-invariant lattice definition of nonabelian chiral gauge theories
problems.plain: A grid version exists for chiral theories with the simplest, electromagnetism-like forces. For the non-commuting forces of the Standard Model it is still missing.
problems.precise: For a 4D anomaly-free chiral gauge theory with nonabelian gauge group (for example SU(5) with 5bar + 10, or one Standard Model generation), construct a lattice regularization with exact gauge invariance at finite lattice spacing, a local action and fermion measure, and the correct continuum limit, extending Luscher's 1999 abelian construction based on Ginsparg-Wilson fermions beyond perturbation theory.
problems.settled_by: An explicit construction with a nonperturbative proof of the locality and gauge invariance of the fermion measure for a nonabelian anomaly-free theory.
problems.status_note: The abelian case was completed in 1999 and the nonabelian case to all orders of perturbation theory in 2000; new proposals in 2024-2026 use domain walls with gauge-field flow and symmetry disentanglers.

topic_review.cite: M. Luscher, Chiral gauge theories revisited, Subnucl. Ser. 38, 41, 2002

problems.title: Continuous symmetric mass generation for sixteen Weyl fermions in 4D
problems.plain: Particles normally get mass by breaking a symmetry. The question is whether strong interactions can give mass to sixteen massless fermions in four dimensions while every symmetry is kept, through a smooth (continuous) change from the massless phase.
problems.precise: For 16 Weyl fermions in 4D (one Standard Model generation with a right-handed neutrino) with interactions preserving Spin(10) or a subgroup with vanishing 't Hooft anomalies, a lattice model may have a gapped phase with no symmetry breaking, no topological order and vanishing bilinear condensates. Determine whether such a phase is reached from the massless phase by a direct continuous transition, which is what a continuum symmetric-mass-generation theory requires.
problems.settled_by: Lattice Monte Carlo of a 4D staggered or domain-wall model showing a direct continuous transition from the massless phase to a gapped phase with unbroken symmetry and no Goldstone modes, or a proof that an intermediate phase is unavoidable.
problems.status_note: Staggered-fermion lattice studies (Butt, Catterall, Hasenfratz and collaborators, 2021-2026) find a massive symmetric phase in 4D; a 2024 gauge-theory study reports a continuous transition, while a 2026 four-fermion study finds the massless and massive symmetric phases separated by an intermediate antiferromagnetic phase.

topic_review.cite: M. Luscher, Chiral gauge theories revisited, Subnucl. Ser. 38, 41, 2002

links.reason: Sixteen-fermion mass generation follows from interaction-reduced fermionic topological classification.

problems.title: Nonperturbative bounds on four-dimensional graviton scattering
problems.plain: In ten and eleven dimensions, bootstrap methods have mapped which graviton-scattering amplitudes are allowed and where string theory lies. In four dimensions the same analysis is blocked by infinities from very low-energy gravitons.
problems.precise: For $D = 4$ $2\to 2$ graviton scattering with Newton constant $G$, determine nonperturbatively (without assuming a weakly coupled UV completion) the allowed range of the leading higher-derivative coefficients ($R^{3}$ and $R^{4}$ terms) in units of the cutoff, using full nonlinear unitarity. The $D = 10$ analogue was mapped by Guerrieri, Penedones, Vieira (Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 081601, 2021); in $D = 4$ the infrared divergences must be handled first.
problems.settled_by: A numerical bootstrap in $D = 4$ with a controlled infrared treatment giving converged bounds.

topic_review.cite: M. Kruczenski, J. Penedones, B. C. van Rees, Snowmass White Paper: S-matrix Bootstrap, arXiv:2203.02421, 2022

problems.title: Bootstrap-ready scattering observables with soft photons and gravitons
problems.plain: In four dimensions, every scattering of charged particles or gravitons emits unlimited numbers of very low-energy photons or gravitons, so the usual scattering amplitude is ill-defined. A replacement object with the properties bootstrap methods need has not been established.
problems.precise: For 4D theories with massless gauge bosons or gravitons, define nonperturbatively asymptotic observables (dressed amplitudes, Faddeev-Kulish states, or inclusive cross sections) that are infrared finite and obey unitarity, analyticity and crossing in a form usable for numerical bootstrap. An answer is such a definition with proofs of these properties, or a demonstration that one of them must fail.
problems.settled_by: A definition with nonperturbative proofs of unitarity, analyticity and crossing, used in a working numerical bootstrap.
problems.status_note: Generalized crossing relations between different asymptotic observables were proven at tree level in 2023 (Caron-Huot, Giroux, Hannesdottir, Mizera, arXiv:2310.12199).

topic_review.cite: M. Kruczenski, J. Penedones, B. C. van Rees, Snowmass White Paper: S-matrix Bootstrap, arXiv:2203.02421, 2022

problems.title: Does large-N QCD lie at the pion bootstrap kink?
problems.plain: Bounds on how massless pions can scatter when the number of colors is large show a sharp corner. Whether QCD with many colors lies exactly at that corner is unknown.
problems.precise: Albert and Rastelli (JHEP 08 (2022) 151) bounded ratios of chiral-Lagrangian Wilson coefficients for massless pions in large-N confining gauge theories, using tree-level meson exchange, crossing, unitarity and Regge behavior, and found a kink on the exclusion boundary. Determine whether the large-N QCD values of these ratios (from lattice QCD at large N or other controlled methods) coincide with the kink, and what meson spectrum the extremal amplitude has.
problems.settled_by: Large-N lattice determination of the relevant Wilson-coefficient ratios compared with the kink location.
problems.status_note: Albert and Rastelli (2022) raised and critically examined the identification; Albert, Henriksson, Rastelli and Vichi (arXiv:2312.15013, 2023) found, under a spin-2 spectral assumption, an extremal amplitude with an apparent Regge trajectory close to real meson masses; no large-N lattice comparison settles it as of 2026.

topic_review.cite: M. Kruczenski, J. Penedones, B. C. van Rees, Snowmass White Paper: S-matrix Bootstrap, arXiv:2203.02421, 2022

problems.title: Allowed region of four-photon low-energy coefficients
problems.plain: At low energy, photons scatter off each other weakly, described by a few numbers. Some combinations of these numbers are bounded by first principles, others appear unconstrained, and the full allowed region is unknown.
problems.precise: For the 4D photon effective theory $L = -F^2/4 + a_1 (F_{mn} F^{mn})^2 + a_2 (F_{mn} Ftilde^{mn})^2 + ...$, with no other light states, determine the region of ($a_1$, $a_2$ and higher coefficients, in units of the cutoff) allowed by full nonlinear unitarity, crossing and analyticity, including strongly coupled UV completions, and identify theories on its boundary. Haring, Hebbar, Karateev, Meineri, Penedones (JHEP 10 (2024) 103) obtained numerical bounds and showed that some coefficients cannot be bounded this way.
problems.settled_by: Converged numerical bootstrap bounds with an identified family of amplitudes on the boundary.
problems.status_note: Numerical bounds exist since 2022; the sharp region and the theories at its edge are not established.

topic_review.cite: M. Kruczenski, J. Penedones, B. C. van Rees, Snowmass White Paper: S-matrix Bootstrap, arXiv:2203.02421, 2022

links.reason: Vacuum birefringence measures four-photon Euler-Heisenberg coefficients that bootstrap bounds constrain.

problems.title: Is 4D flat-space gravity dual to a 3D Carrollian field theory?
problems.plain: An alternative to the celestial sphere places the equivalent description of flat-space gravity on null infinity, the surface reached by outgoing light rays, as a theory in which the speed of light is effectively zero (a Carrollian theory). Whether such a theory exists with its own rules, independent of the gravity calculation, is unknown.
problems.precise: Carrollian holography proposes that the 4D asymptotically flat gravitational S-matrix equals correlators of a sourced 3D conformal Carrollian field theory on null infinity, constrained by BMS Ward identities (Donnay, Fiorucci, Herfray, Ruzziconi 2022). Determine whether an intrinsically defined Carrollian theory exists whose correlators reproduce tree and one-loop graviton amplitudes, and how it relates to the celestial CFT.
problems.settled_by: An intrinsic 3D Carrollian theory whose correlators are computed without reference to the bulk and match 4D graviton amplitudes through one loop, or a proof that no local Carrollian theory can do so.
problems.status_note: The framework and its Ward identities were set up in 2022; no intrinsic dual of Einstein gravity is known.

topic_review.cite: S. Pasterski, M. Pate, A.-M. Raclariu, Celestial Holography, arXiv:2111.11392, 2021

problems.title: Is there a consistent celestial CFT for four-dimensional gravity?
problems.plain: Scattering of particles in flat space can be rewritten as correlations on a sphere at infinity. Whether these correlations form a self-consistent quantum theory on that sphere is unknown.
problems.precise: Celestial holography maps the 4D asymptotically flat S-matrix, via a Mellin transform in energy, to correlators on the celestial sphere. Determine whether for Einstein gravity beyond tree level these correlators form a CFT with a local operator algebra, OPE and state-operator map, and find an intrinsic definition independent of the bulk.
problems.settled_by: An intrinsic 2D construction reproducing loop-level gravitational amplitudes, or a proof that the required CFT axioms fail.
problems.status_note: A top-down dual, a 2D chiral algebra, exists for a self-dual-type theory (Mabuchi gravity coupled to a 4D WZW model) on Burns space (Costello, Paquette, Sharma 2022-2023); full Einstein gravity remains open.

topic_review.cite: S. Pasterski, M. Pate, A.-M. Raclariu, Celestial Holography, arXiv:2111.11392, 2021

links.reason: Soft theorems underlying celestial holography define the charges proposed as soft hair.

problems.title: Holographic dual of quantum gravity in de Sitter space
problems.plain: A universe with positive vacuum energy has no spatial boundary to hold an equivalent quantum theory. Where such a description lives and what it is are unknown.
problems.precise: Find a quantum system whose observables compute those of quantum gravity in asymptotically de Sitter space, for example a Euclidean CFT at future infinity (dS/CFT, Strominger 2001), a static-patch or horizon dual, or double-scaled SYK, reproducing at least the Gibbons-Hawking entropy and the tree-level wavefunction of the universe.
problems.settled_by: A quantum system with a derived dictionary reproducing the Gibbons-Hawking entropy and de Sitter graviton correlators at tree level.
problems.status_note: Proposals based on double-scaled SYK (2022-2025) and on algebras of observables in the static patch (2022) are under debate.

topic_review.cite: S. Pasterski, M. Pate, A.-M. Raclariu, Celestial Holography, arXiv:2111.11392, 2021

problems.title: Microscopic count of de Sitter horizon entropy
problems.plain: The horizon of an expanding universe has an entropy proportional to its area, just like a black hole. Which quantum states it counts is unknown.
problems.precise: The Gibbons-Hawking entropy of a d-dimensional de Sitter horizon is $S = A c^3/(4 G \hbar)$ with $k_B = 1$. Find a statistical system whose state count reproduces S including the one-loop logarithmic correction computed by Anninos, Denef, Law and Sun (2020).
problems.settled_by: A microscopic system with a derived match of the leading area term and the logarithmic correction.
problems.status_note: The static-patch algebra of observables was shown to be of von Neumann type $\mathrm{II}_{1}$ with a maximum-entropy state (Chandrasekaran, Longo, Penington, Witten 2022), without a microscopic count.

topic_review.cite: S. Pasterski, M. Pate, A.-M. Raclariu, Celestial Holography, arXiv:2111.11392, 2021

links.reason: Observer-dependent algebras give de Sitter entropy as an algebraic entropy.

problems.title: Does the flat-space limit of AdS/CFT define the full S-matrix?
problems.plain: Shrinking the curvature of anti-de Sitter space to zero should turn its exact boundary description into flat-space scattering. Whether this works beyond approximations is unknown.
problems.precise: Determine whether the flat-space limit $R_{\mathrm{AdS}} \to \infty$ at fixed string length of $N=4$ super-Yang-Mills correlators (via Mellin amplitudes, Penedones 2010) yields a well-defined nonperturbative $10\mathrm{D}$ type IIB S-matrix, including energies where black holes form.
problems.settled_by: A proof that the limit exists and yields a unitary S-matrix, or an obstruction at high energies.

topic_review.cite: S. Pasterski, M. Pate, A.-M. Raclariu, Celestial Holography, arXiv:2111.11392, 2021

problems.title: Do all six-dimensional superconformal theories arise from F-theory?
problems.plain: A catalog of six-dimensional theories was built from geometric constructions in string theory. Whether every such theory appears in the catalog is unknown.
problems.precise: Heckman, Morrison, Rudelius and Vafa (2015) classified $6\mathrm{D}\,(1,0)$ SCFTs realized by F-theory on elliptically fibered Calabi-Yau threefolds with contractible bases. Determine whether every interacting $6\mathrm{D}\,(1,0)$ SCFT admits such a realization, including frozen phases with $\mathrm{O7}+$ planes, by a field-theoretic completeness argument or a counterexample.
problems.settled_by: A field-theoretic proof that consistency (anomaly cancellation and unitarity on the tensor branch) admits only the geometric list, or an explicit theory outside it.
problems.status_note: Frozen-singularity theories (Bhardwaj, Morrison, Tachikawa, Tomasiello 2018) enlarged the F-theory list; no field-theoretic completeness argument exists.

topic_review.cite: J. J. Heckman, T. Rudelius, Top Down Approach to 6D SCFTs, J. Phys. A 52, 093001, 2019

problems.title: Intrinsic definition of the six-dimensional (2,0) theory
problems.plain: The six-dimensional $(2,0)$ theory, the version with the maximum amount of supersymmetry, is defined only as a limit of a stack of M5-branes, membrane-like objects of M-theory. A definition that stands on its own is missing.
problems.precise: The 6D $N=(2,0)$ superconformal theory of type $A_{N-1}$ is defined as the low-energy limit of N coincident M5-branes or of type IIB string theory on $C^2/Z_N$. Give a self-contained definition independent of string and M-theory (operator algebra and Hilbert space, a UV completion via 5D maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills, deconstruction, or a lattice limit) that reproduces known data: anomaly coefficients scaling as $N^3$, the $W_N$ chiral algebra, and the protected spectrum.
problems.settled_by: A construction from which the $N^{3}$ anomaly scaling and the $W_N$ chiral algebra follow as derived results.
problems.status_note: Proposals that 5D maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills is a complete definition (2010-2011) and deconstruction approaches are not accepted as complete.

topic_review.cite: J. J. Heckman, T. Rudelius, Top Down Approach to 6D SCFTs, J. Phys. A 52, 093001, 2019

problems.title: Microscopic origin of $N^3$ degrees of freedom on M5-branes
problems.plain: A stack of $N$ M5-branes behaves as if it carried about $N^3$ independent quantities, while a stack of $N$ ordinary D-branes carries about $N^2$. Which objects supply the $N^3$ is unknown.
problems.precise: The thermal free energy and anomaly coefficients of the $A_{N-1}$ $(2,0)$ theory scale as $N^{3}$ at large $N$ (Klebanov and Tseytlin 1996 from supergravity). Identify the microscopic degrees of freedom responsible (for example membrane states stretched between triples of M5-branes) and derive the coefficient of $N^{3}$ from them.
problems.settled_by: A microscopic count, in a definition of the theory, that reproduces the coefficient of $N^{3}$ in the anomaly or free energy.

topic_review.cite: J. J. Heckman, T. Rudelius, Top Down Approach to 6D SCFTs, J. Phys. A 52, 093001, 2019

problems.title: Classification of rank-2 four-dimensional $N=2$ superconformal theories
problems.plain: Four-dimensional theories with extra supersymmetry (a symmetry pairing each force particle with a matter particle) can be sorted by the shape of their space of vacua. The sorting is complete only for the simplest case, with one complex dimension.
problems.precise: Classify 4D $N=2$ SCFTs whose Coulomb branch has complex dimension 2 by their scale-invariant special Kahler geometry (fibrations by 2-dimensional abelian varieties, their stratification, and allowed Coulomb branch scaling dimensions), extending the rank-1 classification of Argyres, Lotito, Lu and Martone (2015-2016), and determine which geometries correspond to consistent SCFTs.
problems.settled_by: A proven complete list of rank-2 Coulomb branch geometries with each entry matched to an SCFT or excluded.
problems.status_note: Rank 1 is classified (2016); rank-2 lists (Martone 2021; Kaidi, Martone, Rastelli, Weaver 2022) are not proven complete.

topic_review.cite: J. J. Heckman, T. Rudelius, Top Down Approach to 6D SCFTs, J. Phys. A 52, 093001, 2019

problems.title: Positive geometry for de Sitter correlators of massless fields
problems.plain: A geometric shape, the cosmological polytope, gives the quantum state of the early universe for a simple toy field. Extending it to the fields that matter, such as massless particles and gravitons in an expanding universe, is open.
problems.precise: The cosmological polytope (Arkani-Hamed, Benincasa, Postnikov, 2017) gives wavefunction coefficients of conformally coupled scalars with polynomial interactions in flat space and FRW backgrounds as canonical forms. Find a positive geometry whose canonical form gives tree-level wavefunction coefficients or in-in correlators of massless minimally coupled scalars or gravitons in de Sitter space.
problems.settled_by: An explicit geometry reproducing the known four-point graviton or massless-scalar de Sitter wavefunction coefficients.

topic_review.cite: E. Herrmann, J. Trnka, The SAGEX Review on Scattering Amplitudes, Chapter 7: Positive Geometry of Scattering Amplitudes, J. Phys. A 55 (44), 2022

links.reason: Non-Gaussianity predictions are de Sitter correlators that positive geometry aims to organize.

problems.title: Positive geometry for graviton scattering amplitudes
problems.plain: Gravity amplitudes lack the cyclic ordering of particles that the gauge-theory shapes rely on. No shape whose volume-like form gives graviton scattering is known.
problems.precise: Find a positive geometry whose canonical form equals tree-level n-graviton amplitudes of Einstein gravity or $N=8$ supergravity in $D = 4$ for all helicity sectors, or the loop integrands of $N=8$ supergravity; or prove that gravity amplitudes cannot be canonical forms in the standard sense.
problems.settled_by: An explicit geometry reproducing all tree-level graviton amplitudes, or a proof of impossibility.

topic_review.cite: E. Herrmann, J. Trnka, The SAGEX Review on Scattering Amplitudes, Chapter 7: Positive Geometry of Scattering Amplitudes, J. Phys. A 55 (44), 2022

problems.title: Positive geometry for nonplanar $N=4$ super-Yang-Mills loop integrands
problems.plain: The amplituhedron covers only the planar limit, where the number of colors is infinite. Finite numbers of colors require nonplanar diagrams, and no geometric shape for them is known.
problems.precise: Find a region in a space of kinematic data whose canonical form (the unique differential form with logarithmic singularities on the region's boundaries) equals the subleading-color (nonplanar) or the full color-dressed $L$-loop four-point integrand of $N=4$ super-Yang-Mills; momentum twistors are unavailable because there is no planar ordering. Nonplanar integrands with only logarithmic singularities and no poles at infinity have been constructed at low loop order.
problems.settled_by: An explicit geometry whose canonical form reproduces the known two- and three-loop nonplanar integrands and predicts higher loops.
problems.status_note: No geometry is known as of 2026.

topic_review.cite: E. Herrmann, J. Trnka, The SAGEX Review on Scattering Amplitudes, Chapter 7: Positive Geometry of Scattering Amplitudes, J. Phys. A 55 (44), 2022

problems.title: Geometric origin of the non-supersymmetric Yang-Mills loop integrand
problems.plain: For gluons without supersymmetry, a 2024 construction using curves drawn on surfaces gives a natural loop integrand (the function integrated over loop momenta) in the limit of many colors. Whether it is the volume-like form of an actual geometric shape is not known.
problems.precise: Arkani-Hamed, Cao, Dong, Figueiredo and He (Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 171601, 2025) defined a gauge-invariant, cut-consistent planar (leading-color) Yang-Mills loop integrand using surface kinematics, building on curve-integral formulas for $\operatorname{Tr}\phi^{3}$ theory, with explicit results at one loop for all multiplicities and a simplest two-loop case. Determine whether this integrand, for all multiplicities n and loop orders L in the planar limit, is the canonical form of a positive geometry, and whether a 4D helicity-basis version exists.
problems.settled_by: Construction of a positive geometry with this canonical form, or a proof that the integrand has non-logarithmic singularities incompatible with one.
problems.status_note: The planar integrand was defined in 2024 (published 2025); no positive geometry with this canonical form is known as of 2026.

topic_review.cite: E. Herrmann, J. Trnka, The SAGEX Review on Scattering Amplitudes, Chapter 7: Positive Geometry of Scattering Amplitudes, J. Phys. A 55 (44), 2022

problems.title: Does QCD perturbation theory plus condensates resum to the exact answer?
problems.plain: QCD predictions combine a divergent power series with small corrections from vacuum condensates. Whether this combination, properly resummed, is complete and unambiguous is unknown.
problems.precise: For the Adler function $D(Q^2)$ of massless QCD, determine whether the perturbative series in $\alpha_s(Q^2)$ together with OPE power corrections (condensates such as $\langle \alpha_s G^2\rangle/Q^4$) forms a resurgent transseries whose median resummation equals the exact function, with each condensate uniquely defined once the summation prescription is fixed.
problems.settled_by: A proof in QCD or a controlled large-$N_{f}$ or lattice comparison showing the resummed transseries equals $D(Q^{2})$, or a counterexample term not captured by the OPE.

topic_review.cite: D. Dorigoni, An introduction to resurgence, trans-series and alien calculus, Annals of Physics 409, 167914, 2019

problems.title: Semiclassical origin of the O(N) model trans-series sectors
problems.plain: For solvable two-dimensional theories, the full set of exponentially small corrections to the divergent series has been extracted from the exact solution. Which field configurations of the theory produce each of these corrections is unknown.
problems.precise: For the 2D $O(N)$ nonlinear sigma model with a chemical potential $h$ coupled to a conserved charge, the free energy $F(h)$ follows exactly from the Bethe ansatz, and a full analytic transseries for observables of this type in integrable field theories was derived by Wiener-Hopf methods with median resummation reproducing the exact value (Bajnok, Balog, Vona 2022). For each nonperturbative sector $\exp(-k/\alpha)$ of the $O(N)$ transseries, identify the path-integral saddles, fractional instantons or condensates that produce it, and compute the corresponding coefficients directly from the path integral.
problems.settled_by: A path-integral computation that reproduces at least the leading nonperturbative coefficients of the Bethe-ansatz transseries from identified semiclassical configurations or condensates.
problems.status_note: The full transseries was obtained from the Bethe ansatz (Bajnok, Balog, Vona 2022, arXiv:2212.09416) and extended to all conserved charges in 2025; its semiclassical interpretation remains open.

topic_review.cite: D. Dorigoni, An introduction to resurgence, trans-series and alien calculus, Annals of Physics 409, 167914, 2019

links.reason: The O(N) mass gap and its trans-series describe the same nonperturbative scale.

problems.title: Semiclassical origin of renormalons in asymptotically free theories
problems.plain: The factorial growth of perturbation series in QCD-like theories is linked to singularities called renormalons, which no known classical solution explains. What nonperturbative object cancels their ambiguity is unknown.
problems.precise: In asymptotically free theories ($4\mathrm{D}$ Yang-Mills and QCD, $2\mathrm{D}$ $\mathrm{O}(N)$, $\mathrm{CP}^{N-1}$ and principal chiral models), the Borel transform of perturbation series has renormalon singularities at positions set by the one-loop beta-function coefficient, not matched by any finite-action classical solution. Identify the nonperturbative sectors (saddles, fractional instantons, bions on R^{d-1} x S^1, or OPE condensates) whose imaginary ambiguities cancel the renormalon ambiguities, and demonstrate the cancellation.
problems.settled_by: An explicit computation in at least one asymptotically free theory showing order-by-order cancellation between the renormalon ambiguity and an identified nonperturbative sector.
problems.status_note: Bion proposals (2012) were questioned when their ambiguities did not match renormalon positions in compactified $\mathrm{CP}^{N-1}$ and $\mathrm{O}(N)$ models (2019-2024).

topic_review.cite: D. Dorigoni, An introduction to resurgence, trans-series and alien calculus, Annals of Physics 409, 167914, 2019

links.reason: The top pole mass carries an infrared renormalon ambiguity of order Lambda_QCD.

problems.title: Nonperturbative completion of the string genus expansion
problems.plain: String theory computes processes as a sum over surfaces with more and more holes, and the sum diverges like factorials. Which nonperturbative effects complete it, and whether the result is unique, is known only in toy models and special settings.
problems.precise: String perturbation theory in $g_{s}$ grows like $(2g)!$ at genus $g$ (Shenker 1990), which points to effects of order $\exp(-1/g_{s})$ from D-branes. For the type II superstring in $10\mathrm{D}$ flat space, determine whether the genus expansion of the four-graviton amplitude at fixed kinematics is resurgent, and whether D-instanton sectors give a unique median-resummed result.
problems.settled_by: An exact transseries for the flat-space four-graviton amplitude, with D-instanton coefficients fixed and the resummed result matched to an independent nonperturbative computation.
problems.status_note: Resurgent transseries are known for minimal strings, JT-gravity matrix models and $N=4$ super-Yang-Mills integrated correlators (2021-2024); the flat-space critical superstring amplitude remains open.

topic_review.cite: D. Dorigoni, An introduction to resurgence, trans-series and alien calculus, Annals of Physics 409, 167914, 2019

problems.title: Irreversibility of RG flows on three-dimensional defects
problems.plain: Defects such as impurity lines or surfaces inside a critical material carry their own count of degrees of freedom. This count is proven to drop under coarse-graining for line, surface and four-dimensional defects, but not for three-dimensional ones.
problems.precise: For a conformal defect of dimension $p$ in a unitary d-dimensional CFT with the bulk held fixed, monotonicity under defect RG flows is proven for $p = 1$ (defect entropy; Cuomo, Komargodski, Raviv-Moshe 2021), $p = 2$ (b-theorem; Jensen and O'Bannon 2015, extended to surface defects in 2018) and $p = 4$ (defect a-theorem; Wang 2021). For $p = 3$, prove or refute that the defect contribution to the regularized sphere free energy decreases, as conjectured by Kobayashi, Nishioka, Sato and Watanabe (2018).
problems.settled_by: A proof of monotonicity of the defect sphere free energy for all unitary $p = 3$ defect flows, or a unitary counterexample.
problems.status_note: The naive $b$-theorem was found to fail when the bulk also flows (Shachar, Sinha, Smolkin 2024); the $p = 3$ case with fixed bulk is unproven.

topic_review.cite: T. Nishioka, Entanglement entropy: holography and renormalization group, Rev. Mod. Phys. 90, 035007, 2018

problems.title: Does the sphere free energy decrease along five-dimensional RG flows?
problems.plain: In three dimensions, a number computed by placing the theory on a sphere is proven to drop under coarse-graining (the F-theorem). Whether the analogous number drops in five dimensions is unknown.
problems.precise: For a unitary $d$-dimensional CFT define F~ = sin(pi d/2) log $Z$(S^d), with Z the renormalized partition function on the round sphere (Giombi and Klebanov 2014); in $d = 5$ this is F~ = log Z(S^5). Prove or refute F~_UV > F~_IR for every unitary RG flow between 5D CFTs. The 3D case was proven from strong subadditivity of entanglement entropy (Casini and Huerta 2012); that argument has not been extended to $d = 5$.
problems.settled_by: A general proof for unitary $5\mathrm{D}$ flows, or a unitary $5\mathrm{D}$ flow (for example a $5\mathrm{D}$ SCFT deformed into a gauge theory) with F~_UV <= F~_IR.
problems.status_note: Consistent with free-field, large-N and $\epsilon$-expansion examples (2014 onward); no general proof as of 2026.

topic_review.cite: T. Nishioka, Entanglement entropy: holography and renormalization group, Rev. Mod. Phys. 90, 035007, 2018

problems.title: Does scale invariance imply conformal invariance in four dimensions?
problems.plain: A theory that looks the same at all magnifications usually has a larger symmetry, conformal symmetry. Whether this always holds in four dimensions is not proven.
problems.precise: For a unitary, Poincare-invariant 4D QFT with a well-defined stress tensor, determine whether scale invariance implies conformal invariance nonperturbatively. It is proven in 2D (Polchinski 1988), shown to all orders of perturbation theory in 4D (Luty, Polchinski, Rattazzi; Fortin, Grinstein, Stergiou, 2012), and argued nonperturbatively under assumptions (Dymarsky, Komargodski, Schwimmer, Theisen 2013).
problems.settled_by: A nonperturbative argument without extra assumptions, or a unitary scale-invariant but non-conformal 4D theory.
problems.status_note: Proven to all orders in perturbation theory (2012) and nonperturbatively under extra assumptions (2013); no general proof.

topic_review.cite: T. Nishioka, Entanglement entropy: holography and renormalization group, Rev. Mod. Phys. 90, 035007, 2018

problems.title: Does the a-anomaly decrease along all six-dimensional RG flows?
problems.plain: In two and four dimensions a number counting effective degrees of freedom is proven to drop under coarse-graining. In six dimensions this is proven only for special supersymmetric cases.
problems.precise: In unitary 6D QFT, the Euler coefficient a of the trace anomaly is conjectured to satisfy $a_{UV} > a_{IR}$ for every RG flow between CFTs. The 4D dilaton proof (Komargodski and Schwimmer 2011) does not carry over because the relevant six-derivative dilaton coupling is not sign-definite by unitarity. Prove or refute the inequality for general, including non-supersymmetric, flows.
problems.settled_by: A general argument (dilaton, entanglement or other) establishing $a_{\mathrm{UV}} > a_{\mathrm{IR}}$ in $d = 6$, or a unitary flow with $a_{\mathrm{UV}} \le a_{\mathrm{IR}}$.
problems.status_note: Proven for supersymmetric tensor-branch flows and, in 2023-2025, orbi-instanton Higgs-branch flows; open in general.

topic_review.cite: T. Nishioka, Entanglement entropy: holography and renormalization group, Rev. Mod. Phys. 90, 035007, 2018

problems.title: Is four-dimensional RG flow a gradient flow of the a-function?
problems.plain: In four dimensions a certain count of degrees of freedom is proven to be lower at long distances than at short ones. A stronger claim, that the couplings always move steadily downhill along a height function given by this count, is checked only in perturbation theory.
problems.precise: Jack and Osborn (1990) showed perturbatively that the beta functions $\beta^{j}$ of a 4D renormalizable QFT satisfy $d_{i} a\sim = \chi_{ij}\beta^{j} + (d_{i} w_{j} - d_{j} w_{i})\beta^{j}$ for a function $a\sim(g)$ equal to the a-anomaly at fixed points. Determine whether, beyond perturbation theory, $\chi_{ij}$ is positive definite so that $a\sim$ decreases monotonically along every flow (strong a-theorem). The weak version $a_{\mathrm{UV}} > a_{\mathrm{IR}}$ between fixed points is proven (Komargodski and Schwimmer 2011).
problems.settled_by: A nonperturbative proof that $\chi_{ij}$ is positive definite in unitary 4D QFT, or a unitary flow along which $a\sim$ increases.
problems.status_note: $\chi_{ij}$ is positive at leading orders and $a\sim$ has been constructed to high loop order for general gauge theories (Jack and Poole 2015); the nonperturbative statement is open.

topic_review.cite: T. Nishioka, Entanglement entropy: holography and renormalization group, Rev. Mod. Phys. 90, 035007, 2018

problems.title: Entanglement-geometry relation outside anti-de Sitter space
problems.plain: The rule that entanglement equals area of a surface in the bulk is established for spaces with negative vacuum energy. Whether a version holds in flat or expanding spacetimes is unknown.
problems.precise: Determine whether an analogue of the Ryu-Takayanagi formula $S = \mathrm{Area}/(4 G \hbar)$ for extremal surfaces holds in de Sitter or asymptotically flat quantum gravity, with an identified quantum system whose subregion entropies it computes (candidates include surfaces anchored at horizons or future infinity and timelike entanglement).
problems.settled_by: A derivation of an area formula from a defined dual system in de Sitter or flat space, checked against an independent entropy computation.

topic_review.cite: M. Van Raamsdonk, Building up spacetime with quantum entanglement, Gen. Rel. Grav. 42, 2323, 2010

problems.title: Holographic entropy inequalities for six regions
problems.plain: Entanglement between regions of a holographic system obeys special inequalities that general quantum systems need not obey. The full list is known only up to five regions.
problems.precise: For n boundary regions, the Ryu-Takayanagi entropies of all $2^n - 1$ unions form a polyhedral cone (Bao et al. 2015). Determine the complete list of facets (holographic entropy inequalities) for $n = 6$; the cone is known for $n \le 5$.
problems.settled_by: A complete list of $n = 6$ facets with a proof that each is valid and tight and that no others exist.
problems.status_note: $n = 5$ was completed in 2019; 2024-2026 work computed extreme rays of the 6-party strong-subadditivity-compatible cone and applied reinforcement-learning searches, without a complete 6-party facet list.

topic_review.cite: M. Van Raamsdonk, Building up spacetime with quantum entanglement, Gen. Rel. Grav. 42, 2323, 2010

problems.title: Which conformal field theories have a semiclassical gravity dual?
problems.plain: Only special quantum theories behave as if they described a smooth curved space with ordinary gravity. The exact conditions that single them out are unknown.
problems.precise: Heemskerk, Penedones, Polchinski and Sully (2009) conjectured that a CFT with large central charge $c$ and a large gap $\Delta_{\mathrm{gap}}$ to single-trace operators of spin greater than 2 has a local Einstein-gravity dual. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on CFT data for a semiclassical local bulk, and prove or refute the conjecture.
problems.settled_by: A derivation from CFT axioms showing that large c and a large gap imply bulk locality and Einstein gravity at low energy, or a counterexample.
problems.status_note: Causality and bootstrap bounds (2016-2023) derived suppression of higher-derivative couplings by $\Delta_{\mathrm{gap}}$; a full proof is missing.

topic_review.cite: M. Van Raamsdonk, Building up spacetime with quantum entanglement, Gen. Rel. Grav. 42, 2323, 2010

links.reason: Maximal chaos is a diagnostic of theories with semiclassical gravity duals.

problems.title: Derive full nonlinear Einstein equations from boundary entanglement
problems.plain: Small ripples of spacetime obeying Einstein's equations have been derived from rules about entanglement. The same for strongly curved spacetime has not been done.
problems.precise: The entanglement first law plus the Ryu-Takayanagi formula implies the linearized Einstein equations around AdS (Faulkner, Guica, Hartman, Myers, Van Raamsdonk 2014), extended to second order in 2017. Derive the full nonlinear bulk Einstein equations with matter from CFT entanglement constraints, or identify the additional input required.
problems.settled_by: A derivation of the nonlinear Einstein equations from boundary entropy relations, or a demonstration that extra CFT input is needed.
problems.status_note: Linear order derived in 2014 and second order in 2017; the nonlinear case is open.

topic_review.cite: M. Van Raamsdonk, Building up spacetime with quantum entanglement, Gen. Rel. Grav. 42, 2323, 2010

links.reason: Both rest on generalized entropy linking entanglement and Einstein's equations.

problems.title: Background-independent definition of M-theory
problems.plain: Each known exact definition of string theory assumes a fixed shape of spacetime at infinity. A definition that does not assume a background is missing.
problems.precise: Exact definitions of string and M-theory exist for asymptotically AdS spacetimes (dual CFTs) and for flat space in light-cone frame (BFSS matrix theory), each tied to asymptotic boundary conditions. Find a formulation whose Hilbert space and observables do not presuppose a background and which contains these as special sectors.
problems.settled_by: A formulation from which at least two known exact definitions with different asymptotics are derived as sectors.

topic_review.cite: T. Banks, W. Fischler, S. H. Shenker, L. Susskind, M theory as a matrix model: A conjecture, Phys. Rev. D 55, 5112, 1997

problems.title: Does BFSS matrix theory recover eleven-dimensional Lorentz invariance?
problems.plain: A quantum mechanics of N by N matrices is conjectured to equal M-theory when N becomes infinite. Whether it reproduces full eleven-dimensional relativity beyond protected calculations is unknown.
problems.precise: The BFSS model, $SU(N)$ maximally supersymmetric quantum mechanics, is conjectured to describe M-theory in light-cone frame as $N \to \infty$ with $p^+ = N/R$. Determine whether its amplitudes (graviton scattering) reproduce 11D Lorentz-invariant results beyond terms protected by supersymmetry, i.e. whether the large-N limit at fixed $p^+$ exists and is boost invariant.
problems.settled_by: A large-N computation of an unprotected scattering amplitude in BFSS compared with 11D supergravity or M-theory.
problems.status_note: Agreement holds for supersymmetry-protected terms (1997-1998); work on soft theorems and scattering in BFSS (2023-2025) tests the large-N limit without a full answer.

topic_review.cite: T. Banks, W. Fischler, S. H. Shenker, L. Susskind, M theory as a matrix model: A conjecture, Phys. Rev. D 55, 5112, 1997

problems.title: Nonperturbative content of closed superstring field theory
problems.plain: String field theory writes string theory like an ordinary field theory and fixes many subtle quantities. Whether it defines string theory beyond the weak-coupling series is unknown.
problems.precise: Closed superstring field theory gives a consistent perturbative definition, including D-instanton contributions with fixed normalizations (Sen 2020-2024). Determine whether it admits classical solutions describing distant backgrounds (full background independence) and a nonperturbative formulation beyond the $g_{s}$ expansion.
problems.settled_by: Construction of a classical solution of closed string field theory describing a background at finite distance in moduli space, or a nonperturbative definition of its path integral.
problems.status_note: Background independence is shown only for nearby backgrounds (Sen and Zwiebach, 1993-1994); D-instanton normalizations computed since 2020 match dual predictions.

topic_review.cite: T. Banks, W. Fischler, S. H. Shenker, L. Susskind, M theory as a matrix model: A conjecture, Phys. Rev. D 55, 5112, 1997

problems.title: Worldsheet string theory dual to free $N=4$ super-Yang-Mills
problems.plain: Gauge theory with many colors and no interaction at all should still be equivalent to a string theory in curved space with strings of zero tension. Finding that string theory explicitly would show from first principles how gauge fields turn into strings.
problems.precise: Planar free $N=4\ \operatorname{SU}(N)$ super-Yang-Mills ($g_{\mathrm{YM}} = 0$, $N \to \infty$) should be dual to tensionless type IIB strings on $\mathrm{AdS}_5 x S^5$. For $\mathrm{AdS}_3 x S^3 x T^4$ with one unit of NS-NS flux this was established with a worldsheet theory reproducing the symmetric-orbifold CFT (Eberhardt, Gaberdiel, Gopakumar 2018-2019). Construct the $\mathrm{AdS}_5$ worldsheet theory and show that its genus-zero correlators equal the planar free-field correlators of all single-trace operators.
problems.settled_by: A worldsheet theory whose genus-zero correlators are shown to equal planar free $N=4$ correlators for all single-trace operators, for example by localization of the worldsheet path integral onto free-field Wick contractions.
problems.status_note: Gaberdiel and Gopakumar (2021, arXiv:2104.08263) proposed a worldsheet description whose spectrum matches planar free $N=4$ super-Yang-Mills; correlators have not been derived from it.

topic_review.cite: T. Banks, W. Fischler, S. H. Shenker, L. Susskind, M theory as a matrix model: A conjecture, Phys. Rev. D 55, 5112, 1997

problems.title: Do four expanding spacetime dimensions emerge in the IKKT model?
problems.plain: A model built from ten large matrices is proposed as a complete definition of one string theory. Whether it produces a universe with three large expanding space directions is unknown.
problems.precise: The type IIB (IKKT) matrix model of ten $N$ x N Hermitian bosonic matrices and fermions is proposed as a nonperturbative definition of type IIB string theory. Determine whether its Lorentzian version at large N dynamically generates a smooth expanding $(3+1)$-dimensional spacetime with $\mathrm{SO}(9) \to \mathrm{SO}(3)$ breaking, rather than singular configurations.
problems.settled_by: Large-N simulations of the Lorentzian model with controlled sign-problem treatment showing (or excluding) smooth emergent 3+1 expansion.
problems.status_note: Early Lorentzian simulations (2012) reported three expanding directions; later work found singular Pauli-matrix-like structures tied to approximations, and complex Langevin studies continued through 2025.

topic_review.cite: T. Banks, W. Fischler, S. H. Shenker, L. Susskind, M theory as a matrix model: A conjecture, Phys. Rev. D 55, 5112, 1997

problems.title: Is every anomaly-free six-dimensional supergravity realized in string theory?
problems.plain: Six-dimensional supergravity theories (gravity plus a symmetry between bosons and fermions) can be listed by checking quantum consistency conditions called anomaly cancellation. Whether every theory that passes these checks actually comes from string theory is unknown.
problems.precise: For 6D $N=(1,0)$ supergravity with $T$ tensor multiplets, gauge group $G$ and hypermultiplet content $H$, Green-Schwarz anomaly cancellation restricts $(T, G, H)$. Determine whether every anomaly-free model that meets all known consistency conditions is realized by a string compactification (string universality, Kumar and Taylor 2009), or identify the additional conditions that remove the remainder.
problems.settled_by: A proof that consistency conditions (anomalies, brane-probe unitarity, black-hole arguments) reduce the anomaly-free list exactly to F-theory and heterotic models, or an anomaly-free model shown consistent with no string realization.
problems.status_note: In ten dimensions the unrealized anomaly-free theories were excluded (Adams, DeWolfe, Taylor 2010); in 6D brane-probe unitarity removed some anomaly-free models (Kim, Shiu, Vafa 2019), and anomaly-free models without known string realization remain.

topic_review.cite: M. R. Douglas, S. Kachru, Flux compactification, Rev. Mod. Phys. 79, 733, 2007

problems.title: Does string theory have controlled metastable de Sitter vacua?
problems.plain: Our universe has a small positive vacuum energy. Whether string theory has a calculable solution of this kind that lives long enough is disputed.
problems.precise: Determine whether there exist solutions of string theory, with $\alpha'$ and $g_s$ corrections under control, whose 4D effective potential has a local minimum with $V > 0$ and lifetime longer than the Hubble time, such as KKLT or Large Volume Scenario constructions in type IIB orientifolds with anti-D3-brane uplift.
problems.settled_by: An explicit compactification with all corrections shown to be parametrically small, or a no-go theorem covering the controlled regimes.
problems.status_note: McAllister, Moritz, Nally and Schachner (2024) constructed explicit candidate KKLT de Sitter vacua at leading order in $\alpha'$ and $g_s$; control of higher corrections is disputed.

topic_review.cite: M. R. Douglas, S. Kachru, Flux compactification, Rev. Mod. Phys. 79, 733, 2007

links.reason: String-vacuum explanations of a small positive Lambda need controlled de Sitter vacua.

problems.title: Is the number of string vacua finite?
problems.plain: String theory offers many ways to curl up extra dimensions. Whether the number of distinct low-energy universes is finite is unknown.
problems.precise: Determine whether the set of string compactifications to 4D with a bounded number of light fields and effective theories valid below a fixed cutoff is finite, including whether the number of topologically distinct Calabi-Yau threefolds is finite.
problems.settled_by: A finiteness theorem for all compactifications below a fixed cutoff, or an infinite family of distinct consistent vacua.
problems.status_note: Finiteness of tadpole-bounded flux vacua on a fixed Calabi-Yau orientifold was proven with tame geometry (Bakker, Grimm, Schnell, Tsimerman 2021); finiteness of Calabi-Yau threefold topologies remains open.

topic_review.cite: M. R. Douglas, S. Kachru, Flux compactification, Rev. Mod. Phys. 79, 733, 2007

links.reason: Whether eternal-inflation measures are well defined depends on the vacuum count.

problems.title: Bound on scalar potential slopes in asymptotic field space
problems.plain: A conjecture says that wherever string theory is weakly coupled, the vacuum energy must slope steeply downhill. Whether this holds, and how steep the slope must be, is unknown.
problems.precise: The refined de Sitter conjecture (2018) states that in asymptotic, weakly coupled regions of moduli space, $\mid \operatorname{grad} V \mid \ge c V/M_{P}$ or $\mathrm{min}\ \mathrm{eigenvalue}(\operatorname{grad}\ \operatorname{grad} V) \le -c' V/M_P^{2}$ with c, c' of order 1. Determine whether this holds in all asymptotic regions of string moduli spaces and find the optimal value of c in d dimensions.
problems.settled_by: A proof over all asymptotic limits of string compactifications with the sharp constant, or an explicit asymptotic counterexample.
problems.status_note: Candidate sharp values are $c = 2/\sqrt{(d-1)(d-2)}$ from the trans-Planckian censorship conjecture (Bedroya, Vafa 2019) and $c = 2/\sqrt{d-2}$ (Rudelius 2021), tested in many but not all asymptotic limits (2021-2025).

topic_review.cite: E. Palti, The Swampland: Introduction and Review, Fortschr. Phys. 67, 1900037, 2019

links.reason: The de Sitter conjecture predicts rolling quintessence, that is, evolving dark energy.

problems.title: Is every infinite-distance limit a decompactification or a weak string?
problems.plain: Some parameters of string theory can be pushed infinitely far, and then a tower of particles becomes very light. A conjecture says the light tower is always either extra dimensions opening up or a new weakly interacting string, with no third option.
problems.precise: Emergent string conjecture (Lee, Lerche, Weigand 2019): in any infinite-distance limit in the moduli space of a d-dimensional quantum gravity theory, the leading tower of states becoming massless in Planck units is either a Kaluza-Klein tower (decompactification) or the excitation tower of a unique weakly coupled, asymptotically tensionless critical string. Prove this from general principles or find a limit whose leading tower is of another kind.
problems.settled_by: A derivation from black-hole thermodynamics and unitarity valid for every infinite-distance limit, or an explicit compactification with a light leading tower of another kind.
problems.status_note: Verified in vector-multiplet moduli spaces of M-theory and type IIA on Calabi-Yau threefolds (2019), in 5D supergravity limits (2024), and argued from the black-hole density of states (Bedroya, Mishra, Wiesner 2024); no general proof.

topic_review.cite: E. Palti, The Swampland: Introduction and Review, Fortschr. Phys. 67, 1900037, 2019

problems.title: Absence of global symmetries in quantum gravity outside anti-de Sitter
problems.plain: It is believed that quantum gravity forbids exact global symmetries, symmetries not tied to a force. This is proven only for spaces with negative vacuum energy and in perturbative string theory.
problems.precise: Harlow and Ooguri (2018) proved in AdS/CFT that bulk quantum gravity has no global symmetries and that the gauge charge spectrum is complete. Determine whether the same holds in asymptotically flat and de Sitter quantum gravity, including higher-form and non-invertible global symmetries.
problems.settled_by: A proof using flat-space or de Sitter quantum gravity principles (S-matrix, black hole evaporation, or a dual description), or a counterexample.
problems.status_note: Proven in AdS/CFT (Harlow, Ooguri 2018) and in perturbative string theory (Banks, Dixon 1988); open in flat and de Sitter space.

topic_review.cite: E. Palti, The Swampland: Introduction and Review, Fortschr. Phys. 67, 1900037, 2019

links.reason: The absence of global symmetries in gravity is why Peccei-Quinn quality is threatened.

problems.title: Sharp lower bound on the exponent in the distance conjecture
problems.plain: When a parameter of string theory is moved through a distance $D$, a tower of particles becomes lighter by a factor $\exp(-\lambda D)$. The conjecture is that $\lambda$ can never be smaller than a fixed number set only by the number of spacetime dimensions.
problems.precise: Distance conjecture (Ooguri and Vafa 2006): along a geodesic of length D in moduli space, measured in Planck units, a tower of states has masses $m \sim \exp(-\lambda D)$. Sharpened version (Etheredge, Heidenreich, Kaya, Qiu, Rudelius 2022): the lightest tower obeys $\lambda \ge 1/\sqrt{d-2}$ in d spacetime dimensions. Prove the bound for all infinite-distance limits of string compactifications, or find a limit with $\lambda < 1/\sqrt{d-2}$.
problems.settled_by: A proof over all infinite-distance limits of string compactifications in each $d$, or an explicit limit with $\lambda < 1/\sqrt{d-2}$.
problems.status_note: Proposed in 2022 with the bound preserved under dimensional reduction and saturated in many string and M-theory compactifications.

problems.title: Does the weak gravity conjecture hold in all quantum gravity theories?
problems.plain: The conjecture says gravity must be the weakest force: some particle must feel electric repulsion stronger than its gravitational attraction. Whether this is a law of all quantum gravity theories is unproven.
problems.precise: Weak gravity conjecture (Arkani-Hamed, Motl, Nicolis, Vafa 2006): every U(1) gauge theory coupled to gravity has a state with charge-to-mass ratio at least that of extremal black holes. Determine whether this holds in every consistent quantum gravity theory, and whether the sublattice or tower versions hold.
problems.settled_by: A derivation from general principles (black hole thermodynamics, unitarity, holography), or a consistent theory violating it.
problems.status_note: Shown in perturbative string settings and supported by black-hole arguments; the strongest lattice version fails in some compactifications (2016), leaving sublattice and tower versions.

topic_review.cite: E. Palti, The Swampland: Introduction and Review, Fortschr. Phys. 67, 1900037, 2019

problems.title: Can causal inequalities be violated when spacetime itself is superposed?
problems.plain: Some theoretical processes give correlations that no fixed, or randomly chosen, order of events could explain; these violate causal inequalities. They cannot appear for events localized in an ordinary fixed spacetime; whether a spacetime in superposition, as quantum gravity may allow, can produce them is unknown.
problems.precise: Causal inequalities bound correlations $p(a,b\mid x,y)$ achievable when parties act in a definite or classically random order. With spacetime-localized operations in a fixed acyclic spacetime they cannot be violated (Vilasini and Renner, PRA 2024), and on time-delocalized subsystems they can (Wechs, Branciard, Oreshkov, Nat. Commun. 2023). Determine whether a violation by spacetime-localized operations is possible when the spacetime geometry itself is in superposition (a gravitating source mass in spatial superposition), and give the minimal source mass and coherence time for it.
problems.settled_by: A proof that localized realizations are impossible even with superposed geometry, or an explicit physical protocol with a gravitating source in superposition achieving a violation.
problems.status_note: Fixed-spacetime localized realizations are excluded (Vilasini and Renner, PRA 2024); time-delocalized realizations exist (Wechs et al., 2023); the dynamical-spacetime case is open.

topic_review.cite: Oreshkov, Costa, Brukner, Quantum correlations with no causal order, Nature Communications, 2012

problems.title: Quantum reference frame changes for general and imperfect frames
problems.plain: Describing physics from the viewpoint of a quantum particle needs rules for switching viewpoints. Several frameworks give such rules for idealized frames; for realistic frames such as small quantum clocks they disagree or are undefined.
problems.precise: Construct transformations between quantum reference frames for arbitrary symmetry groups (including non-Abelian, e.g. SU(2) rotations) and non-ideal frames (finite-dimensional, with non-orthogonal orientation states), and prove equivalence or a precise relation between the perspective-neutral (constraint-based), operational and perspectival approaches. An answer is one framework with proofs that each existing one is a special case, or a stated inequivalence.
problems.settled_by: Published theorems relating the frameworks for general groups and non-ideal frames.
problems.status_note: Frameworks for general groups and some non-ideal frames exist; their full equivalence is proved only for restricted classes of frames.

topic_review.cite: Oreshkov, Costa, Brukner, Quantum correlations with no causal order, Nature Communications, 2012

links.reason: Quantum reference frame changes are the tool for relating different relational clock descriptions.

problems.title: Measure quantum time dilation of a clock in a momentum superposition
problems.plain: A moving clock ticks slower by an amount fixed by its speed. If the clock is in a superposition of two speeds, theory predicts an extra effect that no ordinary random mixture of speeds can produce, and no measurement of it has been reported.
problems.precise: For a clock of rest mass m with internal Hamiltonian $H_{\mathrm{clock}}$ whose center of mass is in a coherent superposition of momenta, the mass-energy coupling $H = \sqrt{p^{2} c^{2} + (m c^{2} + H_{\mathrm{clock}})^{2}}$ gives a proper-time distribution that differs from that of the corresponding classical mixture of momenta by a coherence-dependent term (Smith and Ahmadi, Nature Communications 2020). Determine whether atomic or ion clocks can resolve this quantum contribution, the momentum separation and fractional frequency resolution required, and measure it.
problems.settled_by: A clock comparison in which a momentum-superposed clock and a matched classical mixture show the predicted difference in frequency shift.
problems.status_note: Predicted in 2020 (doi:10.1038/s41467-020-18264-4); no measurement was found in the sources checked.

topic_review.cite: Oreshkov, Costa, Brukner, Quantum correlations with no causal order, Nature Communications, 2012

problems.title: Which process matrices are physically realizable?
problems.plain: The mathematics allows many exotic arrangements of operations, but only some can be built with real devices. The task is the exact list, for four or more parties and for processes that cannot be completed into a reversible one.
problems.precise: Wechs, Branciard and Oreshkov (2023) showed that every unitarily extendible tripartite process has a realization on time-delocalized subsystems. Determine (a) whether every unitarily extendible process with $N \ge 4$ parties has such a realization, and (b) whether processes with no unitary extension (no purification), such as the Oreshkov-Costa-Brukner bipartite process, admit any realization within standard quantum theory.
problems.settled_by: A realization theorem for unitarily extendible N-party processes, and a proof or counterexample for non-purifiable processes.
problems.status_note: Tripartite unitarily extendible processes are realizable on time-delocalized subsystems (2023); causally separable processes equal circuits with classical control of causal order (Wechs, Abbott, Branciard, arXiv:2609.20774; for the extensibly causally separable class also Wei and Pang, arXiv:2609.18559, September 2026); $N \ge 4$ and non-purifiable processes are open.

topic_review.cite: Oreshkov, Costa, Brukner, Quantum correlations with no causal order, Nature Communications, 2012

problems.title: Do laboratory quantum switches realize genuinely indefinite causal order?
problems.plain: A quantum switch sends a photon through devices A and B in a superposition of the orders A-then-B and B-then-A. Critics say each device actually acts at two different times, so the order is definite in spacetime and only appears indefinite.
problems.precise: For photonic quantum-switch experiments (operations applied at two distinct times on a time-delocalized subsystem), determine whether the process is causally nonseparable relative to spacetime-localized events, or is a causally ordered circuit on time-delocalized subsystems (Oreshkov, Quantum 2019). An answer is an agreed operational definition of an event and a classification of existing experiments under it.
problems.settled_by: A theorem or consensus definition linking process-matrix nonseparability to localized events, applied to the optical experiments.
problems.status_note: Vilasini and Renner (Phys. Rev. A 110, 022227, 2024) proved that any fixed-spacetime realization uses systems not localized in spacetime and has a fine-grained definite-order description; whether the coarse-grained indefinite order counts as genuine remains disputed.

topic_review.cite: Oreshkov, Costa, Brukner, Quantum correlations with no causal order, Nature Communications, 2012

problems.title: Bell test for temporal order using a mass in superposition
problems.plain: If a heavy mass is in a superposition of two positions, nearby clocks tick at superposed rates, which can put the order of two events in superposition. A proposed Bell-type test would show this order is not fixed in advance by hidden variables.
problems.precise: Zych, Costa, Pikovski and Brukner (Nature Communications 2019) proposed a Bell-type inequality for the temporal order of events controlled by a massive body in spatial superposition. Using the weak-field proper-time difference $\Delta \tau \sim G M \Delta x t / (c^{2} d^{2})$, determine the minimal mass, separation and coherence time for a violation, and demonstrate it.
problems.settled_by: Observation of the predicted violation with a source mass in spatial superposition.

topic_review.cite: Oreshkov, Costa, Brukner, Quantum correlations with no causal order, Nature Communications, 2012

problems.title: Does absence of barren plateaus imply classical simulability?
problems.plain: Variational quantum algorithms tune circuit settings to lower a cost, but most become untrainable because the cost changes exponentially little as the settings vary (a barren plateau). It is conjectured that every circuit family provably free of this flatness can also be imitated by a classical computer, which would remove the point of using it.
problems.precise: For parametrized circuits with loss $L(\theta) = \operatorname{Tr}[O U(\theta) \rho U(\theta)^{\mathrm{dag}}]$ whose gradient variance provably decays at most polynomially in qubit number $n$, is there always a classical algorithm that, after collecting $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ measurement data from a quantum device once, estimates $L(\theta)$ to $1/\operatorname{poly}(n)$ for any $\theta$ in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time? Cerezo et al. (arXiv:2312.09121, Nat. Commun. 16, 7907, 2025) argue yes for known families. An answer is a proof, or a barren-plateau-free family with a hardness proof.
problems.settled_by: A general simulation theorem under the polynomial-gradient-variance assumption, or a counterexample family with a complexity-theoretic hardness proof.

topic_review.cite: R. Orus, Tensor networks for complex quantum systems, Nature Reviews Physics, 2019

problems.title: Efficient contraction of PEPS for gapped two-dimensional ground states
problems.plain: Two-dimensional quantum states can be written compactly as networks of small tensors (PEPS, projected entangled pair states), but extracting numbers from these networks is in general very hard. Whether it becomes easy for physically relevant states with an energy gap is open.
problems.precise: For an injective PEPS of bond dimension $\chi = O(1)$ on an $L$ x L lattice whose parent Hamiltonian is gapped uniformly in L, is there a classical algorithm computing a local expectation value to additive error $\epsilon$ in time $\operatorname{poly}(L, 1/\epsilon)$? Exact contraction of general PEPS is #P-hard (Schuch et al. 2007) and random PEPS are average-case hard to contract (Haferkamp et al. 2020). Schwarz, Buerschaper and Eisert (Phys. Rev. A 95, 060102, 2017, arXiv:1606.06301) give a quasi-polynomial algorithm under additional assumptions (a gapped transfer operator and conditions on the boundary state); the open question is polynomial time from the bulk gap alone.
problems.settled_by: A provably efficient contraction algorithm under the gap assumption, or a hardness proof for gapped injective PEPS.
problems.status_note: Quasi-polynomial contraction is known under extra assumptions (2017); polynomial time from the gap alone is open.

topic_review.cite: R. Orus, Tensor networks for complex quantum systems, Nature Reviews Physics, 2019

problems.title: Photon-loss threshold for classical simulability of Gaussian boson sampling
problems.plain: Gaussian boson sampling sends squeezed light through a large optical network and records where photons arrive; it was used to claim quantum advantage. Losing photons makes the task easier for classical computers, and the loss level at which it becomes easy is not known exactly.
problems.precise: For Gaussian boson sampling with $M$ modes, $K$ single-mode squeezed inputs of squeezing r, a Haar-random interferometer and uniform transmission $\eta$, find the boundary $\eta_c(r, K, M)$ separating classically efficient sampling to fixed total-variation error from sampling hard under standard conjectures, as M, K go to $\infty$ at fixed ratio.
problems.settled_by: A classical algorithm efficient below $\eta_c$ together with a hardness proof above it, for the same scaling family.
problems.status_note: Oh et al. (arXiv:2306.03709, Nature Physics 2024) simulated reported experiments by exploiting their loss; sufficient conditions for hardness of lossy GBS appeared in 2025 (arXiv:2511.07853).

topic_review.cite: R. Orus, Tensor networks for complex quantum systems, Nature Reviews Physics, 2019

problems.title: Finite-size boundary of classical hardness for noisy random circuit sampling
problems.plain: At a fixed error rate per gate, very large random circuits become easy for classical computers, yet the experiments done so far are believed to be hard. Where the crossover lies, in qubit number, depth and noise rate, is not known.
problems.precise: For random circuit sampling with $n$ qubits, depth $D$ and per-gate error $\epsilon$, Aharonov et al. (2023) give a classical algorithm polynomial in $n$ at constant $\epsilon$, with cost exponential in $1/\epsilon$. Determine the best classical cost to reach the experimental linear cross-entropy fidelity $F_{\mathrm{XEB}} \sim \exp(-\epsilon n D)$ as a function of $(n, D, \epsilon)$, and locate the easy-hard boundary for parameters of current experiments ($n \sim 70-100$, $\epsilon \sim 10^{-3}$).
problems.settled_by: Classical algorithms and complexity bounds that place each published experiment on a quantified side of the boundary.
problems.status_note: Google Quantum AI (Nature 2024) reported a noise-driven phase transition in random circuit sampling and placed its experiment in the hard phase; classical simulation efforts continue.

topic_review.cite: R. Orus, Tensor networks for complex quantum systems, Nature Reviews Physics, 2019

links.reason: Both ask which noisy quantum dynamics keep observables accurate yet classically hard.

problems.title: Classical sampling of random circuits with non-unital noise
problems.plain: Noise that scrambles qubits toward randomness makes deep quantum circuits easy to imitate classically. Noise that pushes qubits toward a fixed state, as energy loss does, behaves differently, and whether such noisy circuits can be imitated is open.
